title.zh: 卷4 帝紀第4 煬帝下
title.raw: 卷4 帝紀第4 煬帝下 Volume 4 Annals 4: Emperor Yang 2

sentences.zh: 八年春正月辛巳，大軍集于涿郡。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, on the day xinsi of the first month, the great army assembled at Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year eight, on xinsi day in the first month, the main force gathered at Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書段文振為左候衞大將軍。

translations.literal: Minister of War Duan Wenzhen was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenzhen, Minister of War, was made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 壬午，下詔曰：

translations.literal: On the day renwu, an edict was issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day the emperor promulgated an edict:

sentences.zh: 天地大德，降繁霜於秋令，聖哲至仁，著甲兵於刑典。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth in their great virtue send down heavy frost in the autumn season; the sage and wise in their utmost benevolence set forth armor and weapons in the code of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth in their vast goodness send killing frost with autumn; the sage in supreme humanity records arms in the law of punishment.

sentences.zh: 故知造化之有肅殺，義在無私，帝王之用干戈，蓋非獲已。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that in creation there is stern slaughter, its principle lying in impartiality, and that when emperors and kings employ weapons of war, it is surely not because they wish to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Creation itself holds stern killing, and its justice is impartial; when emperors take up arms, they do so only because they must.

sentences.zh: 版泉、丹浦，莫匪龔行，取亂覆昏，咸由順動。

translations.literal: At Banquan and Danpu, none failed to march in righteous array; overthrowing disorder and toppling darkness all came from acting in accord with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: At Banquan and Danpu every host marched as if to a funeral rite; overthrowing chaos and crushing the benighted all arose from righteous action.

sentences.zh: 況乎甘野誓師，夏開承大禹之業，商郊問罪，周發成文王之志。

translations.literal: How much more so when at Gan Wilds troops were sworn, Xia Qi inherited the enterprise of Great Yu, at the suburbs of Shang guilt was arraigned, and Zhou Fa fulfilled the will of King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: All the more when Xia Qi swore his host at Gan Wilds and carried on Yu's work, and Zhou Fa arraigned guilt outside Shang and fulfilled Wen's design.

sentences.zh: 永監前載，屬當朕躬。

translations.literal: Ever taking the former records as mirror, the task now falls to my person.
translations.idiomatic: Let the past be our mirror: the charge is mine to bear.

sentences.zh: 粵我有隋，誕膺靈命，兼三才而建極，一六合而為家。

translations.literal: Verily our Sui, born to receive the numinous mandate, embracing the three powers established the supreme pole and made the six directions one household.
translations.idiomatic: Our Sui received the sacred mandate, took up heaven, earth, and man to establish the summit of rule, and united the realm into one household.

sentences.zh: 提封所漸，細柳、盤桃之外，聲教爰暨，紫舌、黃枝之域。

translations.literal: Wherever our boundaries extended, beyond Thin Willow and Coiled Peach, our transforming influence reached even the lands of Purple Tongue and Yellow Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Our domains stretched beyond Thin Willow and Pan-Peach, and our civilizing sway reached even to Purple-Tongue and Yellow-Branch lands.

sentences.zh: 遠至邇安，罔不和會，功成治定，於是乎在。

translations.literal: The distant came and the near were at peace; none failed to harmonize and gather; merit was achieved and order settled — therein lay the fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: The far arrived, the near rested easy, all were brought into harmony, and with achievement complete and order settled, the work stood fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 而高麗小醜，迷昏不恭，崇聚勃、碣之間，荐食遼、獩之境。

translations.literal: Yet the petty wretch of Goguryeo, deluded and disrespectful, massed between the Bo and Jie ranges and repeatedly preyed upon the borders of Liao and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty Goguryeo, benighted and insolent, clustered between Bo and Jie and again and again ravaged the Liao and Hui frontier.

sentences.zh: 雖復漢、魏誅戮，巢窟暫傾，亂離多阻，種落還集。

translations.literal: Although Han and Wei had punished and slain them and their nests and lairs were for a time overturned, through turmoil and separation many obstacles arose and the tribes gathered once more.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei had punished them and their strongholds briefly collapsed, but through chaos and distance the clans reassembled.

sentences.zh: [1]萃川藪於往代，播實繁以迄今，眷彼華壤，翦為夷類。

translations.literal: [1] Gathering in river marshes since former ages and spreading their seed abundantly down to the present, they have turned that splendid soil into barbarian territory.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Since old times they have crowded the river marshes and multiplied to this day, carving our fine lands into barbarian country.

sentences.zh: 歷年永久，惡稔既盈，天道禍淫，亡徵已兆。

translations.literal: Years upon years have passed; their wickedness is full; Heaven's Way punishes excess, and the signs of ruin are already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Years have piled up, their evil is ripe, Heaven punishes the licentious, and the omens of extinction are already plain.

sentences.zh: 亂常敗德，非可勝圖，掩慝懷姦，唯日不足。

translations.literal: Disrupting the constant and ruining virtue — it cannot all be plotted against; hiding evil and harboring treachery — not a day passes without more.
translations.idiomatic: They violate order and ruin virtue beyond all reckoning, hiding malice and nursing treachery without cease.

sentences.zh: 移告之嚴，未嘗面受，朝覲之禮，莫肯躬親。

translations.literal: Our stern proclamations they have never received face to face; the rites of court audience they refuse to perform in person.
translations.idiomatic: They never receive our solemn notices in person, and they will not come themselves to pay court.

sentences.zh: 誘納亡叛，不知紀極，充斥邊垂，亟勞烽候，關柝以之不靜，生人為之廢業。

translations.literal: They entice and accept fugitive rebels beyond all limit, fill the border regions, repeatedly wear out the beacon guards, and through the watch-towers peace is lost and the people abandon their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: They shelter deserters without limit, swarm the frontier, exhaust the beacon stations, unsettle the border posts, and drive the people from their work.

sentences.zh: 在昔薄伐，已漏天網，既緩前擒之戮，未即後服之誅，曾不懷恩，翻為長惡，乃兼契丹之黨，虔劉海戍，習靺鞨之服，侵軼遼西。

translations.literal: In former days when we lightly campaigned, the net of Heaven was already loose; having relaxed the punishment of an earlier capture and not immediately inflicted the penalty due a later submission, they did not cherish our grace but turned to lasting evil, joining with the Khitan faction to slaughter the coastal garrisons and adopting Mohe dress to raid west of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Even when we marched lightly before, Heaven's net was already slack; we spared those once taken and did not at once punish those who submitted late, yet they repaid kindness with lasting malice, allied with the Khitan to butcher coastal defenses, and dressed as Mohe to raid western Liao.

sentences.zh: 又青丘之表，咸修職貢，碧海之濱，同稟正朔，遂復奪攘琛賮，遏絕往來，虐及弗辜，誠而遇禍。

translations.literal: Moreover, beyond the Blue Hills all paid their duties and tribute; along the shores of the Blue Sea all received our calendar — yet they again seized and plundered tribute gifts, cut off all coming and going, and their cruelty reached even the innocent, who perished though guilty of nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Blue Hills all kept tribute; along the Blue Sea all accepted our calendar — yet they robbed envoys, blocked the roads, and slaughtered the guiltless.

sentences.zh: 輶軒奉使，爰暨海東，旌節所次，途經藩境，而擁塞道路，拒絕王人，無事君之心，豈為臣之禮！

translations.literal: When envoys in light carriages were sent even to the Eastern Sea, wherever our banners and credentials passed through their border lands, they blocked the roads and rejected the king's men — where is the heart of serving a lord? What manner of subject's rite is this!
translations.idiomatic: Our envoys bound for the Eastern Sea passed through their territory, yet they blocked the roads and refused the throne's officers — this is no mind to serve a sovereign, nor any rite of a subject!

sentences.zh: 此而可忍，孰不可容！

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: If we tolerate this, what outrage could we not endure!

sentences.zh: 且法令苛酷，賦斂煩重，強臣豪族，咸執國鈞，朋黨比周，以之成俗，賄貨如市，寃枉莫申。

translations.literal: Moreover, their laws and orders are harsh and cruel, levies and exactions heavy and frequent; powerful ministers and great clans all grasp the keys of state; factions band together until it becomes custom; bribes flow like a market and wrongs go unredressed.
translations.idiomatic: Their statutes are savage, their taxes crushing; great families hold the reins of power, factions rule by custom, bribes trade like goods in a market, and the wronged find no hearing.

sentences.zh: 重以仍歲災凶，比屋饑饉，兵戈不息，徭役無期，力竭轉輸，身填溝壑。

translations.literal: Added to this are successive years of disaster and calamity, famine in every household, war unceasing, corvée labor without end, strength exhausted in transport, bodies filling ditches and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this come years of disaster, hunger in every home, endless war and corvée, men spent hauling supplies until they fall dead in the ditches.

sentences.zh: 百姓愁苦，爰誰適從？

translations.literal: The common people are bitter and afflicted — to whom can they turn?
translations.idiomatic: The people groan in misery — whom can they follow?

sentences.zh: 境內哀惶，不勝其弊。

translations.literal: Within the borders sorrow and dread are more than they can bear.
translations.idiomatic: Inside their realm grief and despair exceed what men can endure.

sentences.zh: 迴首面內，各懷性命之圖，黃髮稚齒，咸興酷毒之歎。

translations.literal: Turning their faces inward, each cherishes a design for life; gray-haired elders and young children alike sigh at the bitter cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Every man turns inward seeking a way to live; old and young alike lament the savage oppression.

sentences.zh: 省俗觀風，爰屆幽朔，弔人問罪，無俟再駕。

translations.literal: To observe their customs and inspect their winds, I now arrive at You and Shuo; to comfort the people and arraign guilt, there is no need to set out twice.
translations.idiomatic: I come to You and Shuo to read their customs and winds; to succor the people and demand an accounting, one campaign is enough.

sentences.zh: 於是親總六師，用申九伐，拯厥阽危，協從天意，殄茲逋穢，克嗣先謨。

translations.literal: Therefore I shall personally command the six armies and proclaim the nine punitive expeditions, rescue them from peril on the brink, align with Heaven's intent, exterminate these fleeing filth, and fulfill the plans of our forebears.
translations.idiomatic: I shall take command of the six hosts, proclaim the nine chastisements, snatch them from the brink, follow Heaven's will, wipe out this fleeing refuse, and complete the design of our ancestors.

sentences.zh: 今宜授律啟行，分麾屆路，掩勃澥而雷震，歷夫餘以電掃。

translations.literal: Now the armies should receive the laws and set forth, divide their banners and reach their routes, cover the Bo Sea with thunder and sweep through Buyeo like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Now let the armies take their orders and march, divide their flags along their routes, roll over the Bo Sea like thunder, and sweep Buyeo like lightning.

sentences.zh: 比戈按甲，誓旅而後行，三令五申，[2]必勝而後戰。

translations.literal: Resting spears and adjusting armor, they shall swear the host and then advance; thrice ordered and five times admonished, [2] they shall fight only when victory is assured.
translations.idiomatic: Spears lowered and armor set, they shall muster and swear before marching; warned again and again, [2] they shall engage only when sure of victory.

sentences.zh: 左第一軍可鏤方道，第二軍可長岑道，第三軍可海冥道，[3]第四軍可蓋馬道，第五軍可建安道，第六軍可南蘇道，第七軍可遼東道，第八軍可玄菟道，第九軍可扶餘道，第十軍可朝鮮道，第十一軍可沃沮道，第十二軍可樂浪道。

translations.literal: The first army on the left shall take the Roufang route; the second army the Changcen route; the third army the Haiming route; [3] the fourth army the Gaima route; the fifth army the Jian'an route; the sixth army the Nansu route; the seventh army the Liaodong route; the eighth army the Xuantu route; the ninth army the Fuyu route; the tenth army the Chaoxian route; the eleventh army the Woju route; the twelfth army the Lelang route.
translations.idiomatic: Left Wing Army One shall advance by the Roufang route; Two by Changcen; Three by Haiming; [3] Four by Gaima; Five by Jian'an; Six by Nansu; Seven by Liaodong; Eight by Xuantu; Nine by Fuyu; Ten by Chaoxian; Eleven by Woju; Twelve by Lelang.

sentences.zh: 右第一軍可黏蟬道，第二軍可含資道，第三軍可渾彌道，第四軍可臨屯道，第五軍可候城道，第六軍可提奚道，第七軍可踏頓道，第八軍可肅慎道，第九軍可碣石道，第十軍可東暆道，第十一軍可帶方道，第十二軍可襄平道。

translations.literal: The first army on the right shall take the Nianchan route; the second army the Hanzhi route; the third army the Hunmi route; the fourth army the Lintun route; the fifth army the Houcheng route; the sixth army the Tixi route; the seventh army the Tadun route; the eighth army the Sushen route; the ninth army the Jieshi route; the tenth army the Dongyi route; the eleventh army the Daifang route; the twelfth army the Xiangping route.
translations.idiomatic: Right Wing Army One shall advance by the Nianchan route; Two by Hanzhi; Three by Hunmi; Four by Lintun; Five by Houcheng; Six by Tixi; Seven by Tadun; Eight by Sushen; Nine by Jieshi; Ten by Dongyi; Eleven by Daifang; Twelve by Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 凡此眾軍，先奉廟略，駱驛引途，總集平壤。

translations.literal: All these armies shall first follow the strategy laid before the ancestral temple, relaying in rapid succession along their routes to assemble at Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: All these hosts shall first obey the plan set before the temple, press forward along their roads, and converge on Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 莫非如豺如貔之勇，百戰百勝之雄，顧眄則山岳傾頹，叱吒則風雲騰鬱，心德攸同，爪牙斯在。

translations.literal: None are other than warriors bold as wolves and leopards, heroes victorious in a hundred battles; a glance from them topples mountains and hills, a shout from them stirs wind and cloud; their hearts and virtue are as one, and their claws and fangs stand ready.
translations.idiomatic: Each is fierce as wolf or leopard, a veteran of a hundred victories; one look from them would shake the hills, one shout would stir the clouds; of one mind and one will, their teeth and claws are ready.

sentences.zh: 朕躬馭元戎，為其節度，涉遼而東，循海之右，解倒懸於遐裔，問疾苦於遺黎。

translations.literal: I myself shall drive the main army and regulate them, crossing east of the Liao and following the sea's right shore, relieving the inverted hanging of distant lands and inquiring after the sufferings of the remnant people.
translations.idiomatic: I shall lead the main force in person, cross east of the Liao, follow the coast, lift the upside-down suffering of distant peoples, and ask after the woes of the survivors.

sentences.zh: 其外輕齎遊闕，隨機赴響，卷甲銜枚，出其不意。

translations.literal: Beyond this, lightly equipped mobile detachments shall respond as occasion demands, rolling up armor and holding gag between teeth to strike where unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Light raiding columns shall move at need, armor rolled and mouths gagged, to strike from nowhere.

sentences.zh: 又滄海道軍舟艫千里，高帆電逝，巨艦雲飛，橫斷浿江，[4]逕造平壤，島嶼之望斯絕，坎井之路已窮。

translations.literal: Also the Coastal Route Army: ships for a thousand li, high sails flashing like lightning, great vessels flying like clouds, cutting across the Pei River, [4] going straight to Pyongyang — the hope of island strongholds is cut off, the path of the well-trapped is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Coastal Army too shall sail a thousand li of ships, sails high and swift as lightning, great hulls cloudlike on the sea, cut the Pei River, [4] and strike straight for Pyongyang until island redoubts lose all hope and the trapped have no way out.

sentences.zh: 其餘被髮左衽之人，控弦待發，微、盧、彭、濮之旅，不謀同辭。

translations.literal: The rest — men with disheveled hair and left-lapped garments — await the bowstring's release; the hosts of Wei, Lu, Peng, and Pu need no counsel to speak as one.
translations.idiomatic: Others with flowing hair and left-lapped coats stand bow in hand; the forces of Wei, Lu, Peng, and Pu are of one voice without debate.

sentences.zh: 杖順臨逆，人百其勇，以此眾戰，勢等摧枯。

translations.literal: Upholding the righteous against the rebellious, each man fights with the strength of a hundred; with such a host in battle, the force is like snapping dry wood.
translations.idiomatic: Marching with justice against rebellion, every soldier fights as ten; with such an army, victory will be like breaking dead wood.

sentences.zh: 然則王者之師，義存止殺，聖人之教，必也勝殘。

translations.literal: Yet the army of a true king keeps to the principle of halting slaughter; the teaching of the sage must triumph over cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the king's army exists to stop killing, and the sage's teaching must overcome savagery.

sentences.zh: 天罰有罪，本在元惡，人之多僻，脅從罔治。

translations.literal: Heaven's punishment falls on the guilty; its root lies in the chief villain; among the multitude of the perverse, those coerced shall not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven punishes guilt, and the chief villain is the target; among the many who stray, the compelled shall go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 若高元泥首轅門，自歸司寇，即宜解縛焚櫬，弘之以恩。

translations.literal: If Gao Yuan comes with bound hands to the camp gate and submits himself to the minister of justice, he should at once be unbound, the coffin burned, and grace extended to him.
translations.idiomatic: If King Gao Yuan binds himself and comes to the camp gate to surrender to justice, unbind him, burn the coffin of submission, and show him mercy.

sentences.zh: 其餘臣人歸朝奉順，咸加慰撫，各安生業，隨才任用，無隔夷夏。

translations.literal: The remaining subjects who return to court in submission shall all be comforted and reassured, each secure in his livelihood, employed according to talent without distinction between barbarian and Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Other subjects who submit shall be reassured, left to their trades, and employed by merit without regard to barbarian or Han.

sentences.zh: 營壘所次，務在整肅，芻蕘有禁，秋毫勿犯，布以恩宥，喻以禍福。

translations.literal: Wherever camps are pitched, discipline must be strict; fodder-gathering is forbidden and not a hair must be taken; distribute grace and explain fortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Where camps are set, order must be strict; forbid foraging and touch not even a hair; proclaim mercy and warn of ruin.

sentences.zh: 若其同惡相濟，抗拒官軍，國有常刑，俾無遺類。

translations.literal: If any aid the wicked together and resist the official armies, the state has fixed punishments — let none remain.
translations.idiomatic: Those who side with the wicked and resist our troops shall face the fixed penalties of the state until none are left.

sentences.zh: 明加曉示，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Make this clearly known and proclaimed, in accord with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Make this known far and wide, as I intend.

sentences.zh: 總一百一十三萬三千八百，號二百萬，其餽運者倍之。

translations.literal: In total: one million one hundred thirteen thousand eight hundred; styled as two million; those supplying provisions doubled this number.
translations.idiomatic: The total was 1,133,800 men, called up as two million; supply troops doubled that figure.

sentences.zh: 癸未，第一軍發，終四十日，引師乃盡，旌旗亘千里。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, the first army set out; after forty days the armies were all deployed; banners and flags stretched for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day the First Army marched; within forty days the last units had departed; flags and banners stretched a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 近古出師之盛，未之有也。

translations.literal: In recent antiquity there had been nothing like this in the grandeur of a campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Never in recent memory had an expedition matched this in scale.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以右候衞大將軍衞玄為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Right Guard General-in-Chief Wei Xuan was appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day Wei Xuan, General-in-Chief of the Right Guard, was made Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，內史令元壽卒。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Palace Secretary Yuan Shou died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Palace Secretary Yuan Shou died.

sentences.zh: 三月辛卯，兵部尚書、左候衞大將軍段文振卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day xinmao, Minister of War and General-in-Chief of the Left Guard Duan Wenzhen died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinmao day, Duan Wenzhen, Minister of War and General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, died.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，上御師。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, the emperor took command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day the emperor assumed command of the host.

sentences.zh: 甲午，臨戎于遼水橋。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, he reviewed the troops at the Liao River bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day he inspected the army at the bridge over the Liao River.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，大軍為賊所拒，不果濟。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, the great army was blocked by the enemy and failed to cross.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day the main force was stopped by the enemy and could not cross.

sentences.zh: 右屯衞大將軍、左光祿大夫麥鐵杖，武賁郎將錢士雄、孟金叉等，皆死之。

translations.literal: Right Encampment Guard General-in-Chief and Left Grand Master of the Palace Mai Tiezhang, Martial Guard Commanders Qian Shixiong and Meng Jingou, and others all died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Mai Tiezhang, General-in-Chief of the Right Encampment Guard and Left Grand Master of the Palace, and the Martial Guard commanders Qian Shixiong and Meng Jingou, among others, were killed.

sentences.zh: 甲午，[5]車駕渡遼。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, [5] the imperial carriage crossed the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day, [5] the emperor crossed the Liao River.

sentences.zh: 大戰于東岸，擊賊破之，進圍遼東。

translations.literal: A great battle was fought on the eastern bank; the enemy was struck and broken, and the army advanced to besiege Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: On the east bank a great battle was fought; the enemy was routed and the siege of Liaodong began.

sentences.zh: 乙未，[6]大頓，見二大鳥，高丈餘，皜身朱足，遊泳自若。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, [6] the army made a great halt and two large birds were seen, more than a zhang in height, with white bodies and red feet, swimming at ease.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day, [6] during a major halt two great birds appeared, over ten feet tall, white-bodied and red-footed, swimming calmly.

sentences.zh: 上異之，命工圖寫，并立銘頌。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at them and ordered artisans to paint them and erect an inscribed stele in praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished and had them painted and a commemorative stele erected in praise.

sentences.zh: 五月壬午，納言楊達卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day renwu, Censor-in-Chief Yang Da died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renwu day, Censor-in-Chief Yang Da died.

sentences.zh: 于時諸將各奉旨，不敢赴機。

translations.literal: At this time the various generals each received orders and dared not seize opportunities on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile each general held strictly to his orders and would not act on opportunity.

sentences.zh: 既而高麗各城守，攻之不下。

translations.literal: Before long Goguryeo held every city in defense, and attacks could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon every Goguryeo city stood on the defensive, and none could be taken.

sentences.zh: 六月己未，幸遼東，責怒諸將。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiwei, the emperor visited Liaodong and rebuked the generals in anger.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiwei day, he went to Liaodong and furiously upbraided his generals.

sentences.zh: 止城西數里，御六合城。

translations.literal: He halted several li west of the city and took up residence at Liuhe Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped a few li west of the city and lodged at Liuhe Fortress.

sentences.zh: 七月壬寅，宇文述等敗績于薩水，右屯衞將軍辛世雄死之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the day renyin, Yuwen Shu and others were defeated at Salsu River; Right Encampment Guard General Xin Shixiong died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on renyin day, Yuwen Shu and others were routed at the Salsu; Right Encampment Guard General Xin Shixiong was killed.

sentences.zh: 九軍並陷，將帥奔還亡者二千餘騎。

translations.literal: Nine armies were all lost; the commanders fled back with little more than two thousand horsemen surviving.
translations.idiomatic: Nine armies were destroyed; the surviving commanders fled back with barely two thousand riders.

sentences.zh: [7]癸卯，班師。

translations.literal: [7] On the day guimao, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: [7] On guimao day the army turned back.

sentences.zh: 九月庚辰，上至東都。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day gengchen, the emperor arrived at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengchen day, the emperor reached the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔曰：「軍國異容，文武殊用，匡危拯難，則霸德攸興，化人成俗，則王道斯貴。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, an edict was issued: "Military and civil affairs require different forms; martial and literary employments serve different ends. To rescue peril and save hardship brings hegemonic virtue to rise; to transform people and complete custom makes the kingly Way precious.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day an edict declared: "Army and state wear different faces; civil and martial skills serve different ends. Saving the realm from crisis raises hegemonic virtue; shaping custom elevates the kingly Way.

sentences.zh: 時方撥亂，屠販可以登朝，世屬隆平，經術然後升仕。

translations.literal: When the age is still settling disorder, butchers and peddlers may enter court; when the world belongs to long peace, only those versed in the classics may advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: In times of chaos, butchers and peddlers may sit in court; in ages of peace, only the learned may rise in rank.

sentences.zh: 豐都爰肇，儒服無預于周行，建武之朝，功臣不參于吏職。

translations.literal: At the founding of Fengdu, scholars in robes had no part in the court ranks; in the Jianwu reign, meritorious ministers took no share in civil appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengdu was first established, Confucian robes did not walk the court ranks; under Jianwu, men of merit did not hold civil posts.

sentences.zh: 自三方未一，四海交爭，不遑文教，唯尚武功。

translations.literal: Since the three regions were not yet one and the four seas were in mutual contention, there was no leisure for civil teaching — only martial achievement was honored.
translations.idiomatic: While the realm was still divided and the four seas at war, there was no time for letters — only arms were prized.

sentences.zh: 設官分職，罕以才授，班朝治人，乃由勳叙，莫非拔足行陣，出自勇夫，斅學之道，既所不習，政事之方，故亦無取。

translations.literal: Establishing offices and assigning duties rarely followed talent; ordering the court and governing the people proceeded by merit ranking — none were other than men plucked from the ranks, sprung from the brave; the way of learning they had never practiced, and the methods of government they therefore could not employ.
translations.idiomatic: Posts were rarely given for talent; court and people were governed by battle honors — men pulled straight from the ranks, raised from the ranks of fighters who had never studied and therefore knew nothing of administration.

sentences.zh: 是非暗于在己，威福專於下吏，貪冒貨賄，不知紀極，蠹政害民，實由於此。

translations.literal: Right and wrong were dark to themselves, authority and favor were monopolized by subordinate officials, greed and bribes knew no limit, and the corruption of government and harm to the people came from this.
translations.idiomatic: They could not see their own faults, delegated all power to underlings, gorged on bribes without limit, and from this came ruined government and ruined people.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，諸授勳官者，並不得回授文武職事，庶遵彼更張，取類於調瑟，求諸名製，不傷于美錦。

translations.literal: From this time forward, all who receive merit offices shall not be transferred back to civil or military duties, so as to follow that change of tuning and resemble resetting the lute strings, and in seeking proper design not injure the fine brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth no holder of a merit office may be reassigned to civil or military duty — like retuning a lute so the brocade of office is not spoiled.

sentences.zh: 若吏部輒擬用者，御史即宜糾彈。」

translations.literal: If the Ministry of Personnel presumptuously proposes such appointments, the censorate should at once impeach them."
translations.idiomatic: If the Ministry of Personnel proposes such an appointment, the censorate shall impeach at once."

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲寅，工部尚書宇文愷卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day jiayin, Minister of Works Yuwen Kai died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jiayin day, Minister of Works Yuwen Kai died.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，以宗女華容公主嫁于高昌王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jimao, the clanswoman Princess Huarong was married to the King of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jimao day, Princess Huarong, a clanswoman, was given in marriage to the king of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，光祿大夫韓壽卒。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Grand Master of the Palace Han Shou died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day Grand Master of the Palace Han Shou died.

sentences.zh: [8]甲申，敗將宇文述、于仲文等並除名為民，斬尚書右丞劉士龍以謝天下。

translations.literal: [8] On the day jiashen, the defeated generals Yuwen Shu, Yu Zhongwen, and others were all stripped of rank and made commoners; Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Shilong was beheaded to appease the realm.
translations.idiomatic: [8] On jiashen day the defeated generals Yuwen Shu and Yu Zhongwen were stripped of rank and reduced to commoners; Vice Director Liu Shilong was executed to answer to the realm.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大旱，疫，人多死，山東尤甚。

translations.literal: This year there was great drought and pestilence; many people died, especially in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought severe drought and plague; multitudes died, above all in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 密詔江、淮南諸郡閱視民間童女，姿質端麗者，每歲貢之。

translations.literal: A secret edict ordered the commanderies south of the Yangzi and Huai to inspect common families for young girls of fine appearance and present them as tribute each year.
translations.idiomatic: Secret orders went to the Jiang-Huai commanderies to search households for pretty girls and send them up as tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 九年春正月丁丑，徵天下兵，募民為驍果，集于涿郡。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, on the day dingchou of the first month, troops were levied from throughout the realm and commoners were recruited as Elite Striking Forces, assembling at Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year nine, on dingchou day in the first month, the empire was called to arms and civilians enrolled as Elite Striking Forces at Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 壬午，賊帥杜彥冰、王潤等陷平原郡，大掠而去。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, the bandit chiefs Du Yanbing and Wang Run and others seized Pingyuan Commandery, plundered greatly, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day the rebel leaders Du Yanbing and Wang Run took Pingyuan Commandery, looted heavily, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，置折衝、果毅、武勇、雄武等郎將官，以領驍果。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, the posts of Breakthrough, Resolute, Martial Brave, and Heroic Martial commanders were established to command the Elite Striking Forces.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day posts of Breakthrough, Resolute, Martial Brave, and Heroic Martial commanders were created to lead the Elite Striking Forces.

sentences.zh: 乙未，平原李德逸聚眾數萬，稱「阿舅賊」，劫掠山東。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Li Deyi of Pingyuan gathered a host of tens of thousands, styled himself "Uncle Bandit," and plundered Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day Li Deyi of Pingyuan raised tens of thousands, called himself "Uncle the Bandit," and ravaged Shandong.

sentences.zh: 靈武白榆妄，[9]稱「奴賊」，劫掠牧馬，北連突厥，隴右多被其患。

translations.literal: Bai Yuwang of Lingwu, [9] styled "Slave Bandit," plundered horse herds, linked with the Turks to the north, and Longyou suffered greatly from his depredations.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yuwang of Lingwu, [9] styled "Slave the Bandit," raided horse pastures, allied with the Turks in the north, and Longyou bore the brunt of his raids.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍范貴討之，連年不能剋。

translations.literal: General Fan Gui was sent to attack him but for successive years could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: General Fan Gui was dispatched against him but could not defeat him for years.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 己亥，遣代王侑、刑部尚書衞玄鎮京師。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Prince of Dai You and Minister of Punishments Wei Xuan were dispatched to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day Prince You of Dai and Minister of Punishments Wei Xuan were sent to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以右驍騎將軍李渾為右驍衞大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Right Valiant Cavalry General Li Hun was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day Li Hun, Right Valiant Cavalry General, was made General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 二月己未，濟北人韓進洛聚眾數萬為羣盜。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day jiwei, Han Jinluo of Jibei gathered a host of tens of thousands and became a bandit horde.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiwei day, Han Jinluo of Jibei raised tens of thousands and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 壬午，[10]復宇文述等官爵。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, [10] Yuwen Shu and the others had their offices and ranks restored.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day, [10] Yuwen Shu and the others were restored to office and rank.

sentences.zh: 又徵兵討高麗。

translations.literal: Troops were again levied to campaign against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was called to arms again for another campaign against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 三月丙子，濟陰人孟海公起兵為盜，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day bingzi, Meng Haigong of Jiyin raised troops and became a bandit; his followers reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingzi day, Meng Haigong of Jiyin took up arms as a bandit with followers numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，發丁男十萬城大興。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, one hundred thousand adult males were conscripted to fortify Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day a hundred thousand men were levied to build up Daxing.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，幸遼東。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, the emperor visited Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day the emperor set out for Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 以越王侗、民部尚書樊子蓋留守東都。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yue Tong and Minister of the People Fan Zigai were left to guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong of Yue and Minister of the People Fan Zigai were left to hold the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 庚子，北海人郭方預聚徒為盜，[11]自號盧公，眾至三萬，攻陷郡城，大掠而去。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Guo Fangyu of Beihai gathered followers and became a bandit; [11] styling himself Duke Lu, his followers reached thirty thousand; he attacked and seized the commandery seat, plundered greatly, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Guo Fangyu of Beihai raised a band of followers, [11] styled himself Duke Lu, gathered thirty thousand men, stormed the commandery city, looted heavily, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚午，車駕渡遼。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day gengwu, the imperial carriage crossed the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on gengwu day, the emperor crossed the Liao River.

sentences.zh: 壬申，遣宇文述、楊義臣趣平壤。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Yuwen Shu and Yang Yichen were dispatched to press on toward Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Yuwen Shu and Yang Yichen were sent to advance on Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 五月丁丑，熒惑入南斗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day dingchou, the Sparkling Deluder entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingchou day, Mars entered the Southern Dipper constellation.

sentences.zh: 己卯，濟北人甄寶車聚眾萬餘，寇掠城邑。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, Zhen Baoche of Jibei gathered a host of more than ten thousand and raided cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Zhen Baoche of Jibei raised over ten thousand men and raided towns throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 六月乙巳，禮部尚書楊玄感反於黎陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day yisi, Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan rebelled at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yisi day, Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan rose in rebellion at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，玄感逼東都。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Xuangan pressed upon the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Xuangan advanced on the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 河南贊務裴弘策拒之，[12]反為賊所敗。

translations.literal: Henan Assistant Minister Pei Hongce resisted him, [12] but in turn was defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hongce, Henan Assistant Minister, tried to hold him off, [12] but was routed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，兵部侍郎斛斯政奔于高麗。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Vice Minister of War Qisi Zheng fled to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Vice Minister of War Qisi Zheng defected to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 庚午，上班師。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, the emperor withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the emperor ordered the army to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 高麗犯後軍，勑右武衞大將軍李景為後拒。

translations.literal: Goguryeo attacked the rear guard; the emperor ordered Right Martial Guard General-in-Chief Li Jing to serve as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo struck the rear; the emperor appointed Li Jing, General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard, to cover the retreat.

sentences.zh: 遣左翊衞大將軍宇文述、左候衞將軍屈突通等馳傳發兵，以討玄感。

translations.literal: Left Wing Guard General-in-Chief Yuwen Shu, Left Guard General Qu Tu Tong, and others were dispatched by relay post to raise troops and suppress Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard, Qu Tu Tong, Left Guard General, and others were sent by fast courier to raise troops against Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己卯，令所在發人城縣府驛。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jimao, orders were issued throughout to conscript men to fortify counties, prefectures, courier stations, and post houses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jimao day, orders went out to levy men everywhere to fortify counties, prefectures, and post stations.

sentences.zh: 癸未，餘杭人劉元進舉兵反，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, Liu Yuanjin of Yuhang raised troops in rebellion; his followers reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Liu Yuanjin of Yuhang took up arms in rebellion with followers numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 八月壬寅，左翊衞大將軍宇文述等破楊玄感於閿鄉，斬之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day renyin, Left Wing Guard General-in-Chief Yuwen Shu and others defeated Yang Xuangan at Wen Village and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin day, Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard, and others routed Yang Xuangan at Wen Village and executed him.

sentences.zh: 餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: The remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels were all suppressed.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，吳人朱爕、晉陵人管崇擁眾十萬餘，自稱將軍，寇江左。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Zhu Can of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinling held a host of more than one hundred thousand, styled themselves generals, and raided the lands east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day Zhu Can of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinling mustered over a hundred thousand men, called themselves generals, and ravaged the Jiangzuo region.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，制驍果之家蠲免賦役。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, an edict exempted households of Elite Striking Forces from levies and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day an edict exempted Elite Striking Force households from taxes and labor service.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔郡縣城去道過五里已上者，徙就之。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, an edict ordered that where county seats stood more than five li from the road, they should be moved closer.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day an edict commanded that county seats lying more than five li from the highway be relocated nearer to it.

sentences.zh: 戊申，制盜賊籍沒其家。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, an edict was issued that the households of bandits and thieves should be confiscated and registered.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day an edict declared that the property of bandits and thieves would be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，賊帥陳瑱等眾三萬，攻陷信安郡。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, the bandit chief Chen Zhen and others, a host of thirty thousand, attacked and seized Xin'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the bandit leader Chen Zhen and thirty thousand followers stormed Xin'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，司農卿、光祿大夫、葛國公趙元淑以罪伏誅。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Director of the Granaries, Grand Master of the Palace, and Duke of Ge Zhao Yuanshu was executed for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day Zhao Yuanshu, Director of the Granaries, Grand Master of the Palace, and Duke of Ge, was put to death for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 九月己卯，濟陰人吳海流、東海人彭孝才並舉兵為盜，眾數萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jimao, Wu Hailiu of Jiyin and Peng Xiaocai of Donghai both raised troops as bandits; their followers numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jimao day, Wu Hailiu of Jiyin and Peng Xiaocai of Donghai each turned bandit with followers in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，賊帥梁慧尚率眾四萬，陷蒼梧郡。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, the bandit chief Liang Huishang led a host of forty thousand and seized Cangwu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day the bandit leader Liang Huishang with forty thousand men took Cangwu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 甲午，車駕次上谷，以供費不給，上大怒，免太守虞荷等官。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, the imperial carriage halted at Shanggu; because supplies were insufficient, the emperor was greatly enraged and dismissed Prefect Yu He and others from office.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day the emperor stopped at Shanggu; when provisions ran short he flew into a rage and removed Prefect Yu He and others from office.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，東陽人李三兒、向但子舉兵作亂，眾至萬餘。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Li San'er of Dongyang and Xiang Danzi raised troops in revolt; their followers reached more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Li San'er of Dongyang and Xiang Danzi rebelled with over ten thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 閏月己巳，幸博陵。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day jisi, the emperor visited Boling.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jisi day, the emperor traveled to Boling.

sentences.zh: 庚午，上謂侍臣曰：「朕昔從先朝周旋於此，年甫八歲，日月不居，倏經三紀，追惟平昔，不可復希！

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, the emperor said to his attending ministers: "In former days I followed the late emperor in coming and going here; I was only eight years old. Days and months do not stay; suddenly three decades have passed. Looking back on those times, they cannot be hoped for again!
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the emperor told his courtiers: "Long ago I traveled here with the late emperor when I was only eight. Years do not stand still — three decades have rushed by. Those days cannot come again!

sentences.zh: 」言未卒，流涕嗚咽，侍衞者皆泣下沾襟。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, tears streamed down and he sobbed; the attendants and guards all wept until their robes were wet.
translations.idiomatic: He could not finish; tears choked him and he wept aloud, and every attendant and guard wept until his collar was soaked.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁丑，賊帥呂明星率眾數千圍東郡，武賁郎將費青奴擊斬之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day dingchou, the bandit chief Lü Mingxing led a host of several thousand and besieged Dong Commandery; Martial Guard Commander Fei Qingnu struck and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dingchou day, the bandit Lü Mingxing with several thousand men besieged Dong Commandery; Martial Guard Commander Fei Qingnu attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔曰：「博陵昔為定州，地居衝要，先皇歷試所基，王化斯遠，故以道冠豳風，義高姚邑。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, an edict was issued: "Boling was formerly Dingzhou; its land occupies a strategic pass. It was the base where the late emperor tested his rule, and royal transformation spread far from there — therefore its Way crowns the Bin wind and its righteousness surpasses Yao's domain.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day an edict declared: "Boling was once Dingzhou, a place of strategic weight where the late emperor first proved himself and from which his royal influence spread — its virtue outshines the Bin ode, its righteousness exceeds Yao's city.

sentences.zh: 朕巡撫氓庶，爰屆茲邦，瞻望郊廛，緬懷敬止，思所以宣播德澤，覃被下人，崇紀顯號，式光令緒。

translations.literal: I inspect and comfort the common people and now arrive in this land; gazing upon its outskirts and marketplaces, I think with reverence on how to spread virtue and grace, extending it to the people below, raising a glorious title and making this fine legacy shine.
translations.idiomatic: I have come to comfort the people and now stand in this land; looking out over its fields and markets, I seek to spread grace and virtue to all below, ennoble its name, and brighten its legacy.

sentences.zh: 可改博陵為高陽郡。

translations.literal: Boling may be renamed Gaoyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Boling shall be renamed Gaoyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 赦境內死罪已下。

translations.literal: Within the borders, pardon all crimes below capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: All crimes short of death shall be pardoned within the commandery.

sentences.zh: 給復一年。

translations.literal: Grant one year's exemption from levies and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Grant a one-year exemption from taxes and labor service.

sentences.zh: 」於是召高祖時故吏，皆量材授職。

translations.literal: Thereupon former officials from Gaozu's time were summoned and all were given posts according to their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: Former officials who had served under Gaozu were then summoned and given posts suited to their talents.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以納言蘇威為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Censor-in-Chief Su Wei was appointed Grand Master of the State with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Censor-in-Chief Su Wei was made Grand Master of the State with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 朱爕、管崇推劉元進為天子。

translations.literal: Zhu Can and Guan Chong enthroned Liu Yuanjin as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can and Guan Chong proclaimed Liu Yuanjin emperor.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍吐萬緒、魚俱羅討之，連年不能剋。

translations.literal: Generals Tuwann Xu and Yu Juluo were dispatched to suppress them but for successive years could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Tuwann Xu and Yu Juluo were sent against them but could not defeat them for years on end.

sentences.zh: 齊人孟讓、王薄等眾十餘萬，據長白山，攻剽諸郡，清河賊張金稱眾數萬，渤海賊帥格謙自號燕王，孫宣雅自號齊王，眾各十萬，山東苦之。

translations.literal: Meng Rang and Wang Bo of Qi and others, a host of more than one hundred thousand, held Changbai Mountain and raided the commanderies; the Qinghe bandit Zhang Jincheng had a host of tens of thousands; the Bohai bandit chief Ge Qian styled himself Prince of Yan, Sun Xuanya styled himself Prince of Qi — each had a host of one hundred thousand; Shandong suffered greatly from them.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Rang and Wang Bo of Qi held Changbai Mountain with over a hundred thousand men and raided the commanderies; Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe had tens of thousands; Ge Qian of Bohai styled himself Prince of Yan and Sun Xuanya styled himself Prince of Qi, each commanding a hundred thousand — Shandong groaned under their depredations.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，[13]以右候衞將軍郭榮為右候衞大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, [13] Right Guard General Guo Rong was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day, [13] Guo Rong, Right Guard General, was made General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 十一月己酉，右候衞將軍馮孝慈討張金稱於清河，反為所敗，孝慈死之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day jiyou, Right Guard General Feng Xiaoci campaigned against Zhang Jincheng in Qinghe but in turn was defeated by him; Xiaoci died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiyou day, Feng Xiaoci, Right Guard General, attacked Zhang Jincheng in Qinghe but was routed and killed.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲申，車裂玄感弟朝請大夫積善及黨與十餘人，仍焚而揚之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jiashen, Xuangan's younger brother Court Gentleman for Consultation Jishan and more than ten of his associates were torn apart by chariots; their bodies were then burned and the ashes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiashen day, Xuangan's brother Jishan, Court Gentleman for Consultation, and more than ten accomplices were torn apart by chariots, then burned and their ashes scattered.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，扶風人向海明舉兵作亂，[14]稱皇帝，建元白烏。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Xiang Haiming of Fufeng raised troops in revolt, [14] styled himself emperor, and established the era name White Crow.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Xiang Haiming of Fufeng rebelled, [14] declared himself emperor, and adopted the era name White Crow.

sentences.zh: 遣太僕卿楊義臣擊破之。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Stud Yang Yichen was dispatched and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Stud Yang Yichen was sent against him and routed his forces.

sentences.zh: 十年春正月甲寅，以宗女為信義公主，嫁於突厥曷娑那可汗。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year, on the day jiayin of the first month, a clanswoman was made Princess Xinyi and given in marriage to Qaghan Yisafu of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year ten, on jiayin day in the first month, a clanswoman was created Princess Xinyi and married to the Turkish qaghan Yisafu.

translations.literal: For Qaghan Yisafu: the character "suo" — in this book's Biography of Pei Ju and also the Biography of the Western Turks it is written as "sa," a variant in transliteration.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note on Qaghan Yisafu: the name element here written "suo" appears as "sa" in the Biographies of Pei Ju and of the Western Turks — a variant transliteration.

sentences.zh: 二月辛未，詔百僚議伐高麗，數日無敢言者。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinwei, an edict ordered the hundred officials to deliberate on campaigning against Goguryeo; for several days none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinwei day, an edict called on the hundred officials to debate war with Goguryeo; for days no one dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔曰：「竭力王役，致身戎事，咸由徇義，莫匪勤誠，委命草澤，棄骸原野，興言念之，每懷愍惻。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, an edict was issued: "Those who exhaust themselves in royal service and devote their persons to military affairs all follow righteousness; none lack diligence and loyalty. They entrusted their lives to the wild marshes and abandoned their bones on the open plain — speaking of this, I always feel deep compassion.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day an edict declared: "Men who gave their all in royal service and fell in battle did so from loyalty and duty. They died in the wilds and lie unburied on the plain — at the thought I am filled with pity.

sentences.zh: 往年出車問罪，將屆遼濱，廟算勝略，具有進止。

translations.literal: In former years when the army went forth to arraign guilt, it was about to reach the Liao shore; the plans calculated in the temple and the strategy of advance and halt were all in place.
translations.idiomatic: When we marched out in former years to punish guilt, we nearly reached the Liao coast; the temple had settled the strategy of advance and halt.

sentences.zh: 而諒惛凶，罔識成敗，高熲愎很，本無智謀，臨三軍猶兒戲，視人命如草芥，不遵成規，坐貽撓退，遂令死亡者眾，不及埋藏。

translations.literal: Yet Liang was benighted and vicious, knowing nothing of success or failure; Gao Jiong was obstinate and harsh, utterly without wisdom or stratagem — commanding the three armies as if at child's play, treating human lives like grass and stalks, not following established rules, and by sitting idle causing delay — thus the dead were many and could not even be buried.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liang was blind to victory and defeat; Gao Jiong was stubborn and witless — he treated the three armies as a game and human lives as straw, ignored the plan, and by his delay left multitudes dead and unburied.

sentences.zh: 今宜遣使人分道收葬，設祭於遼西郡，立道場一所。

translations.literal: Now envoys should be sent by separate routes to gather and bury the dead, perform sacrifices in Liaoxi Commandery, and establish one Buddhist ritual site.
translations.idiomatic: Now let envoys go by separate routes to collect and bury the dead, offer rites in Liaoxi Commandery, and establish a ritual ground.

sentences.zh: 恩加泉壤，庶弭窮魂之寃，澤及枯骨，用弘仁者之惠。

translations.literal: Grace reaching the yellow springs should quiet the grievances of souls in extremity; favor extending to withered bones should display the benevolence of the humane.
translations.idiomatic: Let grace reach the underworld to still the wronged dead; let mercy touch dry bones and show the humane ruler's kindness.

sentences.zh: 」辛卯，詔曰：

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, an edict was issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day a further edict was promulgated:

sentences.zh: 黃帝五十二戰，成湯二十七征，方乃德施諸侯，令行天下。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor fought fifty-two battles; Cheng Tang launched twenty-seven campaigns — only then did virtue reach the feudal lords and orders run throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor fought fifty-two times; Cheng Tang marched twenty-seven — only then did virtue reach the lords and command run under heaven.

sentences.zh: 盧芳小盜，漢祖尚且親戎，隗囂餘燼，光武猶自登隴，豈不欲除暴止戈，勞而後逸者哉！

translations.literal: Lu Fang was a petty thief, yet Emperor Gao of Han still took the field in person; the embers of Wei Xiao remained, yet Emperor Guangwu still climbed Long himself — was it not because he wished to end violence and halt arms, laboring first so that ease might follow!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fang was a petty bandit, yet Han Gaozu still went to war in person; Wei Xiao's remnant embers remained, yet Guangwu still climbed Long himself — for he meant to end violence and rest only after the labor was done!

sentences.zh: 朕纂成寶業，君臨天下，日月所照，風雨所沾，孰非我臣，獨隔聲教。

translations.literal: I have inherited the precious enterprise and rule as sovereign over the realm; wherever sun and moon shine and wind and rain fall, who is not my subject — yet alone they are cut off from our transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: I have inherited the sacred charge and rule the realm; wherever sun and moon shine and rain falls, all are my subjects — yet Goguryeo alone stands apart from our civilizing sway.

sentences.zh: 蕞爾高麗，僻居荒表，鴟張狼噬，侮慢不恭，抄竊我邊陲，侵軼我城鎮。

translations.literal: That puny Goguryeo, dwelling in remote wilds, spreads like owls and wolves in arrogance and disrespect, plundering our borderlands and raiding our fortified towns.
translations.idiomatic: Petty Goguryeo, tucked away in the wilderness, struts and bites like wolves, scorning our court, raiding our frontier and storming our towns.

sentences.zh: 是以去歲出軍，問罪遼、碣，殪長蛇於玄菟，戮封豕於襄平。

translations.literal: Therefore last year the army went forth to arraign guilt at Liao and Jie, slaying the long serpent at Xuantu and killing the great boar at Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Last year we marched to punish them at Liao and Jie, struck down their long serpent at Xuantu and slaughtered their great boar at Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 扶餘眾軍，風馳電逝，追奔逐北，徑踰浿水，滄海舟楫，衝賊腹心，焚其城郭，污其宮室。

translations.literal: The Fuyu armies, swift as wind and lightning, pursued the fleeing and drove the routed, crossing straight over the Pei River; the coastal ships struck at the enemy's heart, burning their walls and defiling their palaces.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyu columns raced like wind and lightning, chased the broken foe across the Pei River; our ships struck at their heart, burned their walls, and laid waste their palaces.

sentences.zh: 高元伏鑕泥首，送款軍門，尋請入朝，歸罪司寇。

translations.literal: Gao Yuan submitted with iron around his neck and dust on his head, offering sincerity at the army gate; soon he requested to enter court and return to accept judgment from the minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: King Gao Yuan came in chains with dust on his head and offered submission at the camp gate; he then asked to come to court and answer before the minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 朕以許其改過，乃詔班師。

translations.literal: Because I permitted his reform, I then ordered the army to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he would reform, I ordered the army to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 而長惡靡悛，宴安鴆毒，此而可忍，孰不可容！

translations.literal: Yet he persisted in evil without repentance, reveling in ease as if drinking poison — if this can be borne, what cannot be tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he clung to evil and refused to repent, fattening on ease like drinking poison — if we tolerate this, what outrage could we not endure!

sentences.zh: 便可分命六師，百道俱進。

translations.literal: At once the six armies may be ordered forth on a hundred routes together.
translations.idiomatic: Let the six armies now advance together on a hundred roads.

sentences.zh: 朕當親執武節，臨御諸軍，秣馬丸都，觀兵遼水，順天誅於海外，救窮民於倒懸，征伐以正之，明德以誅之，止除元惡，餘無所問。

translations.literal: I shall personally take up the martial standard and command the armies, feed horses at Wandu, review troops at the Liao River, execute Heaven's punishment beyond the seas, rescue the afflicted people from inverted hanging, correct them by punitive expedition, and punish them by bright virtue — removing only the chief villain, with no questions asked of the rest.
translations.idiomatic: I shall take the martial standard in hand, command the hosts in person, water horses at Wandu and review troops on the Liao, carry Heaven's punishment overseas and lift the people from their upside-down plight — only the chief villain shall die; the rest shall go unharmed.

sentences.zh: 若有識存亡之分，悟安危之機，翻然北首，自求多福；

translations.literal: If any recognize the boundary between survival and ruin, perceive the hinge of safety and peril, and suddenly turn north to seek their own greater fortune —
translations.idiomatic: If any see the line between life and death, grasp the turning point of safety and danger, and turn north to save themselves —

sentences.zh: 必其同惡相濟，抗拒王師，若火燎原，刑茲無赦。

translations.literal: But if they aid the wicked together and resist the royal army, like fire spreading over the plain, punishment shall know no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: But those who side with the wicked and resist the throne's army shall be punished without mercy, like fire sweeping a plain.

sentences.zh: 有司便宜宣布，咸使知聞。

translations.literal: The responsible officials should promptly proclaim this so that all may know and hear.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices proclaim this at once so all may hear.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，扶風人唐弼舉兵反，眾十萬，推李弘為天子，[16]自稱唐王。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Tang Bi of Fufeng raised troops in rebellion; his followers numbered one hundred thousand; he enthroned Li Hong as Son of Heaven, [16] and styled himself Prince of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Tang Bi of Fufeng rebelled with a hundred thousand followers, proclaimed Li Hong emperor, [16] and styled himself Prince of Tang.

sentences.zh: 三月壬子，行幸涿郡。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renzi, the emperor traveled to Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renzi day, the emperor set out for Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，次臨渝宮，親御戎服，禡祭黃帝，斬叛軍者以釁鼓。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, he halted at Linyu Palace, personally donned martial garb, performed the military rite sacrifice to the Yellow Emperor, and beheaded a rebel to smear the war drums.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day he stopped at Linyu Palace, put on armor, sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor in the military rite, and beheaded a rebel to consecrate the drums.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛未，彭城賊張大彪聚眾數萬，保懸薄山為盜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day xinwei, the Pengcheng bandit Zhang Dabiao gathered a host of tens of thousands and held Xuanshi Mountain as a bandit stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on xinwei day, the Pengcheng bandit Zhang Dabiao raised tens of thousands and fortified Xuanshi Mountain.

sentences.zh: 遣榆林太守董純擊破，斬之。

translations.literal: Yulin Prefect Dong Chun was dispatched, defeated him, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin Prefect Dong Chun was sent against him, routed his force, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 甲午，車駕次北平。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, the imperial carriage halted at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day the emperor stopped at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 五月庚子，詔舉郡孝悌廉潔各十人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day gengzi, an edict ordered each commandery to recommend ten men each for filial piety, fraternal duty, integrity, and purity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengzi day, an edict called for each commandery to recommend ten men noted for filial piety, brotherliness, integrity, and purity.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，賊帥宋世謨陷琅邪郡。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, the bandit chief Song Shimai seized Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day the bandit leader Song Shimai took Langye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 庚申，延安人劉迦論舉兵反，自稱皇王，建元大世。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, Liu Jialun of Yan'an raised troops in rebellion, styled himself August King, and established the era name Great Age.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Liu Jialun of Yan'an rebelled, declared himself August King, and adopted the era name Great Age.

sentences.zh: 六月辛未，賊帥鄭文雅、林寶護等眾三萬，陷建安郡，太守楊景祥死之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day xinwei, the bandit chiefs Zheng Wenya, Lin Baohu, and others, a host of thirty thousand, seized Jian'an Commandery; Prefect Yang Jingxiang died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinwei day, the bandits Zheng Wenya and Lin Baohu with thirty thousand men took Jian'an Commandery; Prefect Yang Jingxiang was killed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸丑，車駕次懷遠鎮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day guichou, the imperial carriage halted at Huaiyuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on guichou day, the emperor stopped at Huaiyuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，曹國遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, Cao sent envoys presenting local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Cao sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 甲子，高麗遣使請降，囚送斛斯政。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Goguryeo sent envoys requesting surrender and delivered Qisi Zheng bound as a prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Goguryeo sent envoys to sue for peace and delivered the bound fugitive Qisi Zheng.

sentences.zh: 上大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 八月己巳，班師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jisi, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jisi day, the army turned back.

sentences.zh: 庚午，右衞大將軍、左光祿大夫鄭榮卒。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Right Guard General-in-Chief and Left Grand Master of the Palace Zheng Rong died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day Zheng Rong, General-in-Chief of the Right Guard and Left Grand Master of the Palace, died.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁卯，上至東都。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day dingmao, the emperor arrived at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dingmao day, the emperor reached the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 己丑，還京師。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙申，支解斛斯政於金光門外。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day bingshen, Qisi Zheng was dismembered outside the Golden Light Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingshen day, Qisi Zheng was torn limb from limb outside the Golden Light Gate.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，有事於南郊。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, the southern suburban rites were performed.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 己酉，賊帥司馬長安破長平郡。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, the bandit chief Sima Chang'an seized Changping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day the bandit leader Sima Chang'an took Changping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，離石胡劉苗王舉兵反，自稱天子，以其弟六兒為永安王，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, the Lishi Hu Liu Miaowang raised troops in rebellion, styled himself Son of Heaven, and made his younger brother Liu'er Prince of Yong'an; his followers reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Liu Miaowang, a Lishi Hu tribesman, rebelled, declared himself emperor, made his brother Liu'er Prince of Yong'an, and gathered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 將軍潘長文討之，不能剋。

translations.literal: General Pan Changwen was sent to suppress him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: General Pan Changwen was dispatched against him but could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 是月，賊帥王德仁擁眾數萬，保林慮山為盜。

translations.literal: That month, the bandit chief Wang Deren held a host of tens of thousands and fortified Linlu Mountain as a bandit stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: That month the bandit Wang Deren with tens of thousands held Linlu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬申，上如東都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day renshen, the emperor proceeded to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen day, the emperor set out for the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 其日，大赦天下。

translations.literal: On that day, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That same day a general amnesty was declared for the empire.

sentences.zh: 戊子，入東都。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, he entered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day he entered the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，賊帥孟讓眾十餘萬，據都梁宮。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, the bandit chief Meng Rang, a host of more than one hundred thousand, held Duliang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day the bandit Meng Rang with over a hundred thousand men seized Duliang Palace.

sentences.zh: 遣江都郡丞王世充擊破之，盡虜其眾。

translations.literal: Assistant Prefect of Jiangdu Wang Shichong was dispatched, defeated him, and captured his entire host.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdu Assistant Prefect Wang Shichong was sent against him, routed his force, and took every man captive.

sentences.zh: 十一年春正月甲午朔，大宴百僚。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, on the first day jiawu of the first month, a great banquet was held for the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year eleven, on the new moon jiawu day in the first month, the emperor held a great feast for the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 突厥、新羅、靺鞨、畢大辭、訶咄、傳越、烏那曷、波臘、吐火羅、俱慮建、忽論、靺鞨、訶多、沛汗、龜茲、疎勒、于闐、安國、曹國、何國、穆國、畢、衣密、失范延、伽折、契丹等國並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: The Turks, Silla, Mohe, Bida, Hedu, Chuanyue, Wunahuo, Bola, Tuhuoluo, Julujian, Hulun, Mohe, Heduo, Peihan, Kucha, Shule, Khotan, An, Cao, He, Mu, Bi, Yimi, Shifanyan, Jiazhe, Khitan, and other states all sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks, Silla, Mohe, Bida, Hedu, Chuanyue, Wunahuo, Bola, Tuhuoluo, Julujian, Hulun, Mohe, Heduo, Peihan, Kucha, Shule, Khotan, An, Cao, He, Mu, Bi, Yimi, Shifanyan, Jiazhe, Khitan, and other states all sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，武賁郎將高建毗破賊帥顏宣政於齊郡，虜男女數千口。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Martial Guard Commander Gao Jianpi defeated the bandit chief Yan Xuanzheng in Qi Commandery and captured several thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Martial Guard Commander Gao Jianpi routed the bandit Yan Xuanzheng in Qi Commandery and took several thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，大會蠻夷，設魚龍曼延之樂，頒賜各有差。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, a great assembly of barbarians was held; fish-dragon and myriad-extension entertainments were staged, and gifts were distributed in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the emperor held a great feast for the barbarian envoys, staged fish-dragon pageantry, and distributed gifts in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 二月戊辰，賊帥揚仲緒率眾萬餘，攻北平，滑公李景破斬之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day wuchen, the bandit chief Yang Zhongxu led a host of more than ten thousand and attacked Beiping; Duke of Hua Li Jing defeated and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuchen day, the bandit Yang Zhongxu with over ten thousand men attacked Beiping; Li Jing, Duke of Hua, routed and executed him.

sentences.zh: 庚午，詔曰：「設險守國，著自前經，重門禦暴，事彰往策，所以宅土寧邦，禁邪固本。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, an edict was issued: "Setting barriers to defend the state is established in former classics; double gates to repel violence are proven in past strategies — thereby to settle the land and secure the realm, forbid evil and strengthen the root.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day an edict declared: "Defending the state with strategic barriers is ordained in the classics; repelling violence with layered gates is proven in old strategy — to secure the realm, forbid evil, and strengthen the foundation.

sentences.zh: 而近代戰爭，居人散逸，田疇無伍，郛郭不修，遂使遊惰實繁，寇𣤸未息。

translations.literal: Yet in recent generations through warfare, inhabitants scattered and fled; fields lacked organization, outer walls went unrepaired — thus idlers and vagrants grew numerous and bandit raids did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recent wars scattered the people, left fields untended and walls unrepaired, and filled the land with idlers while bandit raids never ceased.

sentences.zh: 今天下平一，海內晏如，宜令人悉城居，田隨近給，使強弱相容，力役兼濟，穿窬無所厝其姦宄，萑蒲不得聚其逋逃。

translations.literal: Now the realm is unified and the empire is at peace; all people should dwell in cities, fields being allotted nearby, so that strong and weak may coexist and labor service be shared — thieves would have no place for their schemes, and fugitives could not gather in the marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is united and the empire at peace, all should live in walled towns with fields assigned nearby, so strong and weak share the burden, thieves find no refuge, and fugitives cannot gather in the wilds.

sentences.zh: 有司具為事條，務令得所。

translations.literal: The responsible officials should draw up detailed regulations and see that all are properly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices draw up detailed rules and ensure fair implementation.

sentences.zh: 」丙子，上谷人王須拔反，自稱漫天王，國號燕，賊帥魏刁兒自稱歷山飛，眾各十餘萬，北連突厥，南寇趙。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Wang Xuba of Shanggu rebelled, styled himself Heavenly King of Man, and took the state name Yan; the bandit chief Wei Diao'er styled himself Flying Over Mount Li; each had a host of more than one hundred thousand, linking with the Turks in the north and raiding Zhao in the south.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day Wang Xuba of Shanggu rebelled as Heavenly King of Man with the state name Yan; the bandit Wei Diao'er styled himself Flying Over Mount Li; each commanded over a hundred thousand men, allied with the Turks in the north, and raided Zhao in the south.

sentences.zh: 五月丁酉，殺右驍衞大將軍、光祿大夫、郕公李渾，將作監、光祿大夫李敏，並族滅其家。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day dingyou, Right Valiant Guard General-in-Chief, Grand Master of the Palace, and Duke of Zheng Li Hun and Director of Palace Construction, Grand Master of the Palace Li Min were executed, and their entire clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingyou day, Li Hun, General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Guard, Grand Master of the Palace, and Duke of Zheng, and Li Min, Director of Palace Construction and Grand Master of the Palace, were executed and their entire families exterminated.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，賊帥司馬長安破西河郡。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, the bandit chief Sima Chang'an seized Xihe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day the bandit Sima Chang'an took Xihe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 己酉，幸太原，避暑汾陽宮。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, the emperor visited Taiyuan and spent the summer at the Fenyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day the emperor went to Taiyuan to escape the heat at Fenyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己亥，淮南人張起緒舉兵為盜，眾至三萬。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jihai, Zhang Qixu of Huainan raised troops as a bandit; his followers reached thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jihai day, Zhang Qixu of Huainan turned bandit with thirty thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，光祿大夫、右禦衞大將軍張壽卒。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Grand Master of the Palace and Right Imperial Guard General-in-Chief Zhang Shou died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day Zhang Shou, Grand Master of the Palace and General-in-Chief of the Right Imperial Guard, died.

sentences.zh: 八月乙丑，巡北塞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day yichou, he inspected the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yichou day, he toured the northern border.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，突厥始畢可汗率騎數十萬，謀襲乘輿，義成公主遣使告變。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Qaghan Shibi of the Turks led several hundred thousand horsemen, planning to surprise the imperial carriage; Princess Yicheng sent envoys to report the plot.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Qaghan Shibi of the Turks led hundreds of thousands of horsemen to ambush the emperor; Princess Yicheng sent word of the plot.

sentences.zh: 壬申，車駕馳幸雁門。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, the imperial carriage hurried to Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day the emperor raced to Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，突厥圍城，官軍頻戰不利。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the Turks besieged the city and the official army repeatedly fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day the Turks besieged the city and the imperial troops lost battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 上大懼，欲率精騎潰圍而出，民部尚書樊子蓋固諫乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly afraid and wished to lead elite cavalry in a breakout; Minister of the People Fan Zigai firmly remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the emperor wanted to break out with elite cavalry; Fan Zigai, Minister of the People, remonstrated firmly and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 齊王暕以後軍保于崞縣。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Yang Jun guarded the rear army at Guo County.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Qi held the rear guard at Guo County.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詔天下諸郡募兵，於是守令各來赴難。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, an edict ordered all commanderies throughout the realm to recruit troops; thereupon prefects and magistrates each came to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day an edict called on every commandery to raise troops; prefects and magistrates rushed to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 九月甲辰，突厥解圍而去。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jiachen, the Turks lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiachen day, the Turks broke the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丁未，曲赦太原、雁門郡死罪已下。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, a partial amnesty was granted in Taiyuan and Yanmen commanderies for all crimes below capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day a partial amnesty was declared in Taiyuan and Yanmen for all crimes short of death.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬戌，上至于東都。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day renxu, the emperor arrived at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on renxu day, the emperor reached the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，彭城人魏騏驎聚眾萬餘為盜，寇魯郡。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Wei Qilin of Pengcheng gathered a host of more than ten thousand as bandits and raided Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day Wei Qilin of Pengcheng raised over ten thousand bandits and raided Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 壬申，賊帥盧明月聚眾十餘萬，寇陳、汝間。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, the bandit chief Lu Mingyue gathered a host of more than one hundred thousand and raided between Chen and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day the bandit Lu Mingyue with over a hundred thousand men raided the Chen-Ru region.

sentences.zh: 東海賊帥李子通擁眾度淮，自號楚王，建元明政，寇江都。

translations.literal: The Donghai bandit chief Li Zitong led his host across the Huai, styled himself Prince of Chu, established the era name Bright Governance, and raided Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The Donghai bandit Li Zitong crossed the Huai with his host, declared himself Prince of Chu, adopted the era name Bright Governance, and raided Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯，賊帥王須拔破高陽郡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day yimao, the bandit chief Wang Xuba seized Gaoyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yimao day, the bandit Wang Xuba took Gaoyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊寅，有大流星如斛，墜明月營，破其衝車。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day wuyin, a great meteor the size of a grain-measure fell into Lu Mingyue's camp and smashed his assault chariots.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuyin day, a great meteor the size of a bushel fell on Lu Mingyue's camp and destroyed his siege engines.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔民部尚書樊子蓋發關中兵，討絳郡賊敬盤陀、柴保昌等，經年不能剋。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, an edict ordered Minister of the People Fan Zigai to dispatch Guanzhong troops to suppress the Jiang Commandery bandits Jing Panto, Chai Baochang, and others; for a full year they could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day an edict ordered Fan Zigai, Minister of the People, to send Guanzhong troops against the Jiang Commandery bandits Jing Panto and Chai Baochang; after a year they still could not defeat them.

sentences.zh: 譙郡人朱粲擁眾數十萬，寇荊襄，僭稱楚帝，建元昌達。

translations.literal: Zhu Can of Qiao Commandery held a host of several hundred thousand, raided Jing and Xiang, presumptuously styled himself Emperor of Chu, and established the era name Flourishing Reach.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can of Qiao Commandery commanded hundreds of thousands, ravaged Jing and Xiang, declared himself Emperor of Chu, and adopted the era name Flourishing Reach.

sentences.zh: 漢南諸郡多為所陷焉。

translations.literal: Many commanderies south of the Han were seized by him.
translations.idiomatic: Many commanderies south of the Han fell to him.

sentences.zh: 十二年春正月甲午，雁門人翟松柏起兵於靈丘，眾至數萬，轉攻傍縣。
