translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year, on the day jiawu of the first month, Zhai Songbai of Yanmen raised troops at Lingqiu; his followers reached tens of thousands and he turned to attack neighboring counties.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year twelve, on jiawu day in the first month, Zhai Songbai of Yanmen rebelled at Lingqiu with tens of thousands and raided neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 二月己未，真臘國遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day jiwei, Chenla sent envoys presenting local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiwei day, Chenla sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 甲子夜，有二大鳥似鵰，飛入大業殿，止于御幄，至明而去。

translations.literal: At night on the day jiazi, two large birds resembling eagles flew into the Daye Hall, alighted on the imperial canopy, and departed at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi night two great eagle-like birds flew into the Daye Hall, settled on the imperial canopy, and left at dawn.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，[17]東海賊盧公暹率眾萬餘，保于蒼山。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, [17] the Donghai bandit Lu Gongxian led a host of more than ten thousand and fortified Cang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day, [17] the Donghai bandit Lu Gongxian with over ten thousand men held Cang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁巳，顯陽門災。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day dingsi, the Xianyang Gate burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on dingsi day, the Xianyang Gate caught fire.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，魏刁兒所部將甄翟兒復號歷山飛，眾十萬，轉寇太原。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Zhen Zhai'er, a subordinate general of Wei Diao'er, again styled himself Flying Over Mount Li; his host numbered one hundred thousand and he turned to raid Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day Zhen Zhai'er, a lieutenant of Wei Diao'er, again styled himself Flying Over Mount Li, gathered a hundred thousand men, and raided Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 將軍潘長文討之，反為所敗，長文死之。

translations.literal: General Pan Changwen was sent to suppress him but in turn was defeated by him; Changwen died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: General Pan Changwen was dispatched against him but was routed and killed.

sentences.zh: 五月丙戌朔，日有蝕之，既。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day bingxu, there was a solar eclipse; it was total.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the new moon bingxu day, there was a total eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，大流星隕于吳郡，為石。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, a great meteor fell in Wu Commandery and became stone.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day a great meteor fell in Wu Commandery and turned to stone.

sentences.zh: 壬午，[18]上於景華宮徵求螢火，得數斛，夜出遊山，放之，光徧巖谷。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, [18] at Jinghua Palace the emperor requisitioned fireflies, obtaining several hu; at night he went out to tour the mountains, released them, and their light filled the cliffs and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day, [18] at Jinghua Palace the emperor collected fireflies by the bushel; that night he toured the mountains and released them until the cliffs and valleys glowed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬戌，民部尚書、光祿大夫濟北公樊子蓋卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day renxu, Minister of the People, Grand Master of the Palace, and Duke of Jibei Fan Zigai died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on renxu day, Fan Zigai, Minister of the People, Grand Master of the Palace, and Duke of Jibei, died.

sentences.zh: [19]甲子，幸江都宮，以越王侗、光祿大夫段達、太府卿元文都、檢校民部尚書韋津、右武衞將軍皇甫無逸、右司郎盧楚等總留後事。

translations.literal: [19] On the day jiazi, the emperor visited the Jiangdu Palace; Prince of Yue Tong, Grand Master of the Palace Duan Da, Director of the Imperial Storehouse Yuan Wendu, Acting Minister of the People Wei Jin, Right Martial Guard General Huangfu Wuyi, and Right Department Gentleman Lu Chu and others were put in overall charge of remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: [19] On jiazi day the emperor went to the Jiangdu Palace; Prince Tong of Yue, Duan Da, Yuan Wendu, Wei Jin, Huangfu Wuyi, Lu Chu, and others were left in charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 奉信郎崔民象以盜賊充斥，於建國門上表，諫不宜巡幸。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Cui Minxiang, because bandits filled the land, submitted a memorial at the Jianguo Gate remonstrating that the tour should not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Cui Minxiang, citing the bandit plague, memorialized at the Jianguo Gate that the emperor should not continue the tour.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，先解其頤，乃斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged; first his jaw was cut off, then he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, had his jaw cut off, then beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，馮翊人孫華自號總管，舉兵為盜。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Sun Hua of Fufeng styled himself Chief Commandant and raised troops as a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Sun Hua of Fufeng styled himself Chief Commandant and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 高涼通守洗珤徹舉兵作亂，嶺南溪洞多應之。

translations.literal: Assistant Administrator of Gaoliang Xian Baoche raised troops in revolt; many stream valleys in Lingnan responded.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Baoche, Assistant Administrator of Gaoliang, rebelled, and many Lingnan hill tribes joined him.

sentences.zh: 己巳，熒惑守羽林，月餘乃退。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, the Sparkling Deluder guarded the Feathered Forest constellation and did not withdraw for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day Mars lingered in the Feathered Forest constellation for over a month.

sentences.zh: 車駕次汜水，奉信郎王愛仁以盜賊日盛，諫上請還西京。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage halted at Sishui, Attendant Gentleman Wang Airen, because bandits grew daily, remonstrated with the emperor to return to the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Sishui, Attendant Gentleman Wang Airen, citing the worsening bandit crisis, urged the emperor to return to the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 上怒，斬之而行。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, beheaded him, and continued on his way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him executed and pressed on.

sentences.zh: 八月乙巳，賊帥趙萬海眾數十萬，自恒山寇高陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day yisi, the bandit chief Zhao Wanhai, a host of several hundred thousand, from Heng Mountain raided Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yisi day, the bandit Zhao Wanhai with hundreds of thousands of men raided Gaoyang from Heng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 壬子，有大流星如斗，出王良閣道，聲如隤牆。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, a great meteor the size of a dipper emerged from the Wangliang Pass Way; its sound was like a collapsing wall.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day a great meteor the size of the Big Dipper burst from the Wangliang Pass Way with a sound like a falling wall.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，大流星如甕，出羽林。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, a great meteor the size of a jar emerged from the Feathered Forest constellation.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day a great meteor the size of a jar emerged from the Feathered Forest constellation.

sentences.zh: 九月丁酉，東海人杜揚州、沈覔敵等作亂，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day dingyou, Du Yangzhou of Donghai, Shen Midí, and others raised a revolt; their followers reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingyou day, Du Yangzhou of Donghai, Shen Midí, and others rebelled with tens of thousands of followers.

sentences.zh: 右禦衞將軍陳稜擊破之。

translations.literal: Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng was dispatched and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng was sent against them and routed them.

sentences.zh: 戊午，有二枉矢出北斗魁，委曲蛇形，注於南斗。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, two crooked arrows emerged from the Dipper's head, winding in serpent form and pointing toward the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day two crooked comets issued from the Dipper's head in serpentine curves toward the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，安定人荔非世雄殺臨涇令，舉兵作亂，自號將軍。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Li Feishixiong of Anding killed the magistrate of Linjing, raised troops in revolt, and styled himself General.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Li Feishixiong of Anding killed the magistrate of Linjing, rebelled, and styled himself General.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己丑，開府儀同三司、左翊衞大將軍、光祿大夫、許公宇文述薨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day jichou, Grand Master of the State with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies, Left Wing Guard General-in-Chief, Grand Master of the Palace, and Duke of Xu Yuwen Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jichou day, Yuwen Shu, Grand Master of the State with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies, General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard, Grand Master of the Palace, and Duke of Xu, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸未，鄱陽賊操天成舉兵反，[20]自號元興王，建元始興，攻陷豫章郡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day guiwei, the Poyang bandit Cao Tiancheng raised troops in rebellion, [20] styled himself Prince of Yuanxing, established the era name Initial Flourish, and seized Yuzhang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guiwei day, the Poyang bandit Cao Tiancheng rebelled, [20] styled himself Prince of Yuanxing, adopted the era name Initial Flourish, and took Yuzhang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以右翊衞大將軍來護兒為開府儀同三司、行左翊衞大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, Right Wing Guard General-in-Chief Lai Huer was appointed Grand Master of the State with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies and Acting Left Wing Guard General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day Lai Huer, General-in-Chief of the Right Wing Guard, was made Grand Master of the State with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies and Acting General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，鄱陽人林士弘自稱皇帝，國號楚，建元太平，攻陷九江、廬陵郡。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Lin Shihong of Poyang styled himself emperor, took the state name Chu, established the era name Great Peace, and seized Jiujiang and Luling commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Lin Shihong of Poyang declared himself emperor, named his state Chu, adopted the era name Great Peace, and took Jiujiang and Luling commanderies.

sentences.zh: 唐公破甄翟兒於西河，虜男女數千口。

translations.literal: The Duke of Tang defeated Zhen Zhai'er in Xihe and captured several thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang routed Zhen Zhai'er in Xihe and took several thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 十三年春正月壬子，齊郡賊杜伏威率眾渡淮，攻陷歷陽郡。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year, on the day renzi of the first month, the Qi Commandery bandit Du Fuwei led his host across the Huai and seized Liyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year thirteen, on renzi day in the first month, the Qi Commandery bandit Du Fuwei crossed the Huai and took Liyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，勃海賊竇建德設壇於河間之樂壽，自稱長樂王，建元丁丑。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, the Bohai bandit Dou Jiande set up an altar at Leshou in Hejian, styled himself Prince of Changle, and established the era name Dingchou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day the Bohai bandit Dou Jiande raised an altar at Leshou in Hejian, declared himself Prince of Changle, and adopted the era name Dingchou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，賊帥徐圓朗率眾數千，破東平郡。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, the bandit chief Xu Yuanlang led a host of several thousand and seized Dongping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the bandit Xu Yuanlang with several thousand men took Dongping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 弘化人劉企成聚眾萬餘人為盜，[21]傍郡苦之。

translations.literal: Liu Qicheng of Honghua gathered a host of more than ten thousand as bandits; [21] neighboring commanderies suffered greatly from them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qicheng of Honghua raised over ten thousand bandits; [21] neighboring commanderies groaned under their raids.

sentences.zh: 二月壬午，朔方人梁師都殺郡丞唐世宗，據郡反，自稱大丞相。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day renwu, Liang Shidu of Shuofang killed Assistant Prefect Tang Shizong, seized the commandery in rebellion, and styled himself Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renwu day, Liang Shidu of Shuofang killed Assistant Prefect Tang Shizong, seized the commandery, and styled himself Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 遣銀青光祿大夫張世隆擊之，反為所敗。

translations.literal: Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace Zhang Shilong was dispatched to attack him but in turn was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shilong, Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace, was sent against him but was routed.

sentences.zh: 戊子，賊帥王子英破上谷郡。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the bandit chief Wang Ziying seized Shanggu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day the bandit Wang Ziying took Shanggu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 己丑，馬邑校尉劉武周殺太守王仁恭，舉兵作亂，北連突厥，自稱定楊可汗。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Mayi Commandant Liu Wuzhou killed Prefect Wang Rengong, raised troops in revolt, linked with the Turks in the north, and styled himself Qaghan Dingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day Liu Wuzhou, Commandant of Mayi, killed Prefect Wang Rengong, rebelled, allied with the Turks in the north, and styled himself Qaghan Dingyang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，賊帥李密、翟讓等陷興洛倉。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, the bandit chiefs Li Mi and Zhai Rang and others seized Xingluo Granary.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day the bandits Li Mi and Zhai Rang took Xingluo Granary.

sentences.zh: 越王侗遣武賁郎將劉長恭、光祿少卿房崱擊之，反為所敗，死者十五六。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong dispatched Martial Guard Commander Liu Changgong and Vice Director of the Masters of Ceremony Fang Ze to attack them but in turn was defeated; fifteen or sixteen out of ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong of Yue sent Martial Guard Commander Liu Changgong and Vice Director of the Masters of Ceremony Fang Ze against them but they were routed; five or six out of every ten were killed.

sentences.zh: 庚子，李密自號魏公，稱元年，開倉以振羣盜，眾至數十萬，河南諸郡相繼皆陷焉。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Li Mi styled himself Duke of Wei, proclaimed year one, opened the granaries to relieve the bandit hosts, and his followers reached several hundred thousand; commanderies of Henan fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Li Mi styled himself Duke of Wei, proclaimed a new reign, opened the granaries to feed the rebels, gathered hundreds of thousands, and one Henan commandery after another fell.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，劉武周破武賁郎將王智辯于桑乾鎮，智辯死之。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Liu Wuzhou defeated Martial Guard Commander Wang Zhibian at Sanggan Garrison; Zhibian died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day Liu Wuzhou routed Martial Guard Commander Wang Zhibian at Sanggan Garrison and killed him.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午，廬江人張子路舉兵反。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day wuwu, Zhang Zilu of Lujiang raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuwu day, Zhang Zilu of Lujiang rebelled.

sentences.zh: 遣右禦衞將軍陳稜討平之。

translations.literal: Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng was dispatched and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng was sent against him and suppressed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，賊帥李通德眾十萬，寇廬江，左屯衞將軍張鎮州擊破之。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, the bandit chief Li Tongde, a host of one hundred thousand, raided Lujiang; Left Encampment Guard General Zhang Zhenzhou defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day the bandit Li Tongde with a hundred thousand men raided Lujiang; Zhang Zhenzhou, General of the Left Encampment Guard, routed him.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸未，金城校尉薛舉率眾反，自稱西秦霸王，建元秦興，攻陷隴右諸郡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day guiwei, Jincheng Commandant Xue Ju led his host in rebellion, styled himself Overlord of Western Qin, established the era name Qin Flourish, and seized the commanderies of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on guiwei day, Xue Ju of Jincheng rebelled, styled himself Overlord of Western Qin, adopted the era name Qin Flourish, and overran the Longyou commanderies.

sentences.zh: 己丑，賊帥孟讓，夜入東都外郭，燒豐都市而去。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, the bandit chief Meng Rang at night entered the outer wall of the Eastern Capital, burned Fengdu Market, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day the bandit Meng Rang broke into the outer wall of the Eastern Capital at night, burned Fengdu Market, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，李密陷迴洛東倉。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Li Mi seized Huiluo East Granary.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Li Mi took Huiluo East Granary.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，賊帥房憲伯陷汝陰郡。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, the bandit chief Fang Xianbo seized Runan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day the bandit Fang Xianbo took Runan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是月，光祿大夫裴仁基、淮陽太守趙佗等並以眾叛歸李密。

translations.literal: That month, Grand Master of the Palace Pei Renji, Huaiyang Prefect Zhao Tuo, and others all defected with their hosts to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: That month Grand Master of the Palace Pei Renji, Huaiyang Prefect Zhao Tuo, and others defected with their troops to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 五月辛酉，夜有流星如甕，墜於江都。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day xinyou, at night a meteor the size of a jar fell at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinyou night, a meteor the size of a jar fell at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 甲子，唐公起義師於太原。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the Duke of Tang raised a righteous army at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the Duke of Tang raised a righteous army at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，突厥數千寇太原，唐公擊破之。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, several thousand Turks raided Taiyuan; the Duke of Tang defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day several thousand Turks raided Taiyuan; the Duke of Tang routed them.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬子，熒惑守積屍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day renzi, the Sparkling Deluder guarded the Heap of Corpses constellation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on renzi day, Mars entered the Heap of Corpses constellation.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，武威人李軌舉兵反，攻陷河西諸郡，自稱涼王，建元安樂。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Li Gui of Wuwei raised troops in rebellion, seized the commanderies of Hexi, styled himself King of Liang, and established the era name Secure Joy.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Li Gui of Wuwei rebelled, overran the Hexi commanderies, declared himself King of Liang, and adopted the era name Secure Joy.

sentences.zh: 八月辛巳，唐公破武牙郎將宋老生於霍邑，斬之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day xinsi, the Duke of Tang defeated Martial Guard Commander Song Laosheng at Huoyi and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinsi day, the Duke of Tang routed Martial Guard Commander Song Laosheng at Huoyi and executed him.

sentences.zh: 九月己丑，[22]帝括江都人女寡婦，以配從兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jichou, [22] the emperor requisitioned unmarried women and widows of Jiangdu to assign to the attendant soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jichou day, [22] the emperor seized unmarried women and widows of Jiangdu and assigned them to his attendant soldiers.

sentences.zh: 是月，武陽郡丞元寶藏以郡叛歸李密，與賊帥李文相攻陷黎陽倉。

translations.literal: That month, Wuyang Assistant Prefect Yuan Baozang defected with his commandery to Li Mi and together with the bandit chief Li Wenxiang seized Liyang Granary.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wuyang Assistant Prefect Yuan Baozang surrendered his commandery to Li Mi and, with the bandit Li Wenxiang, took Liyang Granary.

sentences.zh: 彗星見於營室。

translations.literal: A comet appeared in the Encampment constellation.
translations.idiomatic: A comet was seen in the Encampment constellation.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁亥，太原楊世洛聚眾萬餘人，寇掠城邑。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day dinghai, Yang Shiluo of Taiyuan gathered a host of more than ten thousand and raided cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dinghai day, Yang Shiluo of Taiyuan raised over ten thousand men and raided towns.

sentences.zh: 丙申，羅令蕭銑以縣反，鄱陽人董景珍以郡反，迎銑於羅縣，號為梁王，攻陷傍郡。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Magistrate of Luo Xiao Xian rebelled with his county; Dong Jingzhen of Poyang rebelled with his commandery and welcomed Xian at Luo County, enthroning him as Prince of Liang; neighboring commanderies were seized.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Magistrate Xiao Xian of Luo rebelled with his county; Dong Jingzhen of Poyang rebelled with his commandery, welcomed Xian at Luo County, and proclaimed him Prince of Liang; neighboring commanderies fell.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，武賁郎將高毗敗濟北郡賊甄寶車於𡽳山。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Martial Guard Commander Gao Pi defeated the Jibei Commandery bandit Zhen Baoche at Qiu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Martial Guard Commander Gao Pi routed the Jibei bandit Zhen Baoche at Qiu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙辰，唐公入京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day bingchen, the Duke of Tang entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingchen day, the Duke of Tang entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，遙尊帝為太上皇，立代王侑為帝，改元義寧。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, the emperor was honored from afar as Retired Emperor; Prince of Dai You was established as emperor and the era name changed to Yining.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day the emperor was honored from afar as Retired Emperor; Prince You of Dai was enthroned and the era name changed to Yining.

sentences.zh: 上起宮丹陽，將遜于江左。

translations.literal: The emperor began building a palace at Danyang, intending to withdraw to the lands east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor began building a palace at Danyang, planning to retreat to the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 有烏鵲來巢幄帳，驅不能止。

translations.literal: Crows and magpies came to nest in the tent canopy; driven away, they would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Crows and magpies nested in the imperial tent; though driven off, they kept returning.

sentences.zh: 熒惑犯太微。

translations.literal: The Sparkling Deluder encroached upon the Supreme Palace constellation.
translations.idiomatic: Mars encroached upon the Supreme Palace constellation.

sentences.zh: 有石自江浮入于揚子。

translations.literal: A stone floated from the river into the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: A stone floated up from the river into the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 日光四散如流血。

translations.literal: Sunlight scattered in all directions like flowing blood.
translations.idiomatic: Sunlight scattered in all directions like blood.

sentences.zh: 上甚惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly detested these omens.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply troubled by these portents.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，右屯衞將軍宇文化及，武賁郎將司馬德戡、元禮，監門直閣裴虔通，將作少監宇文智及，武勇郎將趙行樞，鷹揚郎將孟景，[23]內史舍人元敏，符璽郎李覆、牛方裕，千牛左右李孝本、弟孝質，直長許弘仁、薛世良，城門郎唐奉義，醫正張愷等，以驍果作亂，入犯宮闈。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, Right Encampment Guard General Yuwen Huaji, Martial Guard Commanders Sima Dekan and Yuan Li, Gate Guard Attendant Pei Qiantong, Assistant Director of Palace Construction Yuwen Zhiji, Martial Brave Commander Zhao Xingshu, Hawk-Raising Commander Meng Jing, [23] Palace Secretary Attendant Yuan Min, Seal and Credential Attendants Li Fu and Niu Fangyu, Thousand-Ox Guards Li Xiaoben and his younger brother Xiaozhi, Attendant Supervisors Xu Hongren and Xue Shiliang, Gate Gentleman Tang Fengyi, Chief Physician Zhang Kai, and others raised a revolt with the Elite Striking Forces and entered to violate the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year two, Yuwen Huaji, General of the Right Encampment Guard, Sima Dekan and Yuan Li, Martial Guard commanders, Pei Qiantong, Gate Guard Attendant, Yuwen Zhiji, Assistant Director of Palace Construction, Zhao Xingshu, Meng Jing, [23] Yuan Min, Palace Secretary Attendant, Li Fu and Niu Fangyu, Seal Attendants, Li Xiaoben and his brother Xiaozhi, Thousand-Ox Guards, Xu Hongren and Xue Shiliang, Attendant Supervisors, Tang Fengyi, Gate Gentleman, Zhang Kai, Chief Physician, and others mutinied with the Elite Striking Forces and stormed the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 上崩于溫室，時年五十。

translations.literal: The emperor died in the Warm Chamber; he was fifty years old.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died in the Warm Chamber at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 蕭后令宮人撤牀簀為棺以埋之。

translations.literal: Empress Xiao ordered palace women to remove bed mats and use them as a coffin for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiao had palace women strip bed mats to make a coffin and bury him.

sentences.zh: 化及發後，右禦衞將軍陳稜奉梓宮於成象殿，葬吳公臺下。

translations.literal: After Huaji departed, Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng escorted the imperial coffin to the Chengxian Hall and buried it below the Terrace of Duke Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji left, Chen Leng, Right Imperial Guard General, conveyed the coffin to Chengxian Hall and buried it below the Terrace of Duke Wu.

sentences.zh: 發斂之始，容貌若生，眾咸異之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the exhumation and reburial, his appearance was as if alive; all marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: When the body was first exhumed, his face looked as if he were still alive; all who saw it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 大唐平江南之後，改葬雷塘。

translations.literal: After the Great Tang pacified Jiangnan, he was reburied at Lei Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang pacified the south, he was reburied at Lei Tang.

sentences.zh: 初，上自以藩王，次不當立，每矯情飾行，以釣虛名，陰有奪宗之計。

translations.literal: In the beginning, because he was a prince by enfeoffment and by order of birth not the one who should succeed, he constantly feigned sentiment and adorned his conduct to fish for empty reputation, secretly harboring a design to seize the succession.
translations.idiomatic: At first, knowing himself a mere enfeoffed prince and not the heir by birth order, he constantly played at virtue to win hollow praise while secretly plotting to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 時高祖雅信文獻皇后，而性忌妾媵。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu greatly trusted Empress Wenxian, who by nature was jealous of concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then trusted Empress Wenxian above all, and she was fiercely jealous of rival consorts.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇內多嬖幸，以此失愛。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong kept many favorites within his household and for this reason lost favor.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong kept many favorites and thereby lost the empress's favor.

sentences.zh: 帝後庭有子，皆不育之，示無私寵，取媚於后。

translations.literal: When the emperor had sons in his inner quarters, he would not raise any of them, showing no partial favor in order to win the empress's approval.
translations.idiomatic: When sons were born in his inner quarters, he refused to raise them, feigning impartiality to please the empress.

sentences.zh: 大臣用事者，傾心與交。

translations.literal: With powerful ministers who held office, he gave his whole heart in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated powerful ministers with every show of devotion.

sentences.zh: 中使至第，無貴賤，皆曲承顏色，申以厚禮。

translations.literal: When palace envoys came to his residence, regardless of rank, he would all bend to their mood and extend generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys of every rank found him obliging and lavish with gifts.

sentences.zh: 婢僕往來者，無不稱其仁孝。

translations.literal: Servants and maidservants who came and went all praised his benevolence and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Every servant who passed through his household praised his benevolence and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 又常私入宮掖，密謀於獻后，楊素等因機構扇，遂成廢立。

translations.literal: He also often entered the inner palace in secret to plot with Empress Xian; Yang Su and others fanned the flames as occasion arose, and thus the deposition and enthronement were accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He often stole into the inner palace to plot with Empress Xian; Yang Su and others seized the moment, and the heir was deposed.

sentences.zh: 自高祖大漸，暨諒闇之中，烝淫無度，山陵始就，即事巡遊，以天下承平日久，士馬全盛，慨然慕秦皇、漢武之事。

translations.literal: From when Gaozu fell gravely ill through the period of mourning, he indulged in incest without limit; as soon as the imperial tomb was completed, he set out on tours, and because the realm had long been at peace and troops and horses were at full strength, he sighed with longing for the deeds of Qin Shihuang and Emperor Wu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozu's death through the mourning period he indulged in licentious excess; the tomb was barely finished when he began touring, and seeing the realm long at peace and the armies strong, he yearned to emulate Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi.

sentences.zh: 乃盛治宮室，窮極侈靡，召募行人，分使絕域。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly expanded the palace buildings to the utmost extravagance, recruited travelers, and dispatched them to distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: He vastly expanded the palaces to extravagant extremes, recruited travelers, and sent them to the ends of the earth.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃至者，厚加禮賜，有不恭命，以兵擊之。

translations.literal: When the various barbarians arrived, he richly bestowed gifts and rewards; those who did not respect his commands he attacked with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys were richly rewarded; those who defied his orders were attacked.

sentences.zh: 盛興屯田於玉門、柳城之外。

translations.literal: He greatly promoted garrison farming beyond Yumen and Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded military colonies beyond Yumen and Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 課天下富室，益市武馬，匹直十餘萬，富強坐是凍餒者十家而九。

translations.literal: He levied the wealthy households throughout the realm to purchase additional war horses at more than one hundred thousand per horse; of the strong and rich, nine out of ten households suffered cold and hunger because of this.
translations.idiomatic: He taxed the empire's wealthy to buy war horses at over a hundred thousand per mount; nine out of ten prosperous households were ruined by cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 帝性多詭譎，所幸之處，不欲人知。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was much given to cunning and deceit; the places he favored visiting he did not wish people to know.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was cunning by nature and kept his destinations secret.

sentences.zh: 每之一所，輒數道置頓，四海珍羞殊味，水陸必備焉，求市者無遠不至。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, he would set up halts on several routes; delicacies and rare flavors from the four seas, by land and water, were all provided; those who sought to sell came from no distance too far.
translations.idiomatic: Every destination had multiple relay routes; delicacies from land and sea were supplied from every quarter; merchants traveled from the ends of the earth to sell.

sentences.zh: 郡縣官人，競為獻食，豐厚者進擢，疎儉者獲罪。

translations.literal: County and prefecture officials competed to present food; those who gave generously were promoted, those who were sparing were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials competed to offer feasts; the lavish were promoted, the frugal were punished.

sentences.zh: 姦吏侵漁，內外虛竭，頭會箕斂，人不聊生。

translations.literal: Corrupt officials preyed on the people; inside and outside the government were drained empty; levies were scraped together with rakes and baskets, and the people could not survive.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials plundered until the state was hollow; taxes were squeezed from every source and the people could not live.

sentences.zh: 于時軍國多務，日不暇給，帝方驕怠，惡聞政事，冤屈不治，奏請罕決。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were many and daily tasks could not all be completed; the emperor was arrogant and negligent, hated to hear of government, left wrongs unredressed, and rarely decided on submitted petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Military and civil affairs overwhelmed the court, yet the emperor grew arrogant and idle, refused to hear petitions, left injustices unresolved, and rarely decided submitted business.

sentences.zh: 又猜忌臣下，無所專任，朝臣有不合意者，必構其罪而族滅之。

translations.literal: He also suspected his ministers and entrusted no one exclusively; when any court official displeased him, he would fabricate crimes and exterminate the clan.
translations.idiomatic: He suspected every minister and trusted no one; any courtier who displeased him was framed and his clan exterminated.

sentences.zh: 故高熲、賀若弼先皇心膂，參謀帷幄，張衡、李金才藩邸惟舊，績著經綸，或惡其直道，或忿其正議，求其無形之罪，加以刎頸之誅。

translations.literal: Thus Gao Jiong and He Ruo Bi, the late emperor's heart and backbone who plotted in the command tent, and Zhang Heng and Li Jincai, old associates of the princely residence whose achievements were outstanding in statecraft — some he hated for their straight path, some he resented for their upright counsel — seeking crimes without form, he added the punishment of cutting the throat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong and He Ruo Bi, the late emperor's closest counselors, and Zhang Heng and Li Jincai, old companions of his princely days — some he hated for their blunt honesty, some for their upright remonstrance — were killed on invented charges.

sentences.zh: 其餘事君盡禮，謇謇匪躬，無辜無罪，橫受夷戮者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The rest who served their lord with full rite, who were upright and devoted, innocent and without guilt, yet perished in extermination — they cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Countless others who served loyally and spoke honestly were slaughtered without cause — too many to record.

sentences.zh: 政刑弛紊，賄貨公行，莫敢正言，道路以目。

translations.literal: Government and punishments were lax and disordered, bribes walked openly in the streets, none dared speak straight, and people looked at one another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Government collapsed, bribes ruled openly, no one dared speak truth, and men met each other's eyes in silence on the road.

sentences.zh: 六軍不息，百役繁興，行者不歸，居者失業。

translations.literal: The six armies did not rest; a hundred corvées flourished; those who marched did not return, those who stayed lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The six armies never rested, a hundred labors multiplied, those who marched never came home, and those who stayed lost their trades.

sentences.zh: 人飢相食，邑落為墟，上不之恤也。

translations.literal: People in hunger ate one another; settlements became ruins; the emperor did not pity them.
translations.idiomatic: The starving fed on one another, villages became wasteland, and the emperor did not care.

sentences.zh: 東西遊幸，靡有定居，每以供費不給，逆收數年之賦。

translations.literal: He toured east and west without fixed residence; whenever supplies were insufficient, he collected taxes for several years in advance.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered east and west without rest; whenever supplies ran short, he collected several years' taxes in advance.

sentences.zh: 所至唯與後宮流連躭湎，惟日不足，招迎姥媼，朝夕共肆醜言，又引少年，令與宮人穢亂，不軌不遜，以為娛樂。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he only lingered with the inner palace in drunken indulgence, never satisfied with the day; he summoned old women to join him morning and evening in vile speech, and also brought in young men to have them commit lewd disorder with palace women — improper and insolent — as his entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he stopped he drank with the harem until dawn, summoned old women to talk obscenely with him, and brought in young men to debauch palace women for sport.

sentences.zh: 區宇之內，盜賊蜂起，劫掠從官，屠陷城邑，近臣互相掩蔽，隱賊數不以實對。

translations.literal: Within the realm bandits swarmed like bees; they plundered the emperor's attendants and slaughtered and seized cities; close officials covered for one another and reported bandit numbers untruthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed across the realm, robbed the emperor's escort, and stormed cities; courtiers lied to one another about the numbers.

sentences.zh: 或有言賊多者，輒大被詰責，各求苟免，上下相蒙，每出師徒，敗亡相繼。

translations.literal: If anyone said the bandits were many, he would be severely rebuked; each sought to escape blame by deceit; superiors and subordinates deceived one another; whenever armies went forth, defeat and destruction followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who reported many bandits was savagely rebuked; officials lied to save themselves; every campaign ended in defeat.

sentences.zh: 戰士盡力，必不加賞，百姓無辜，咸受屠戮。

translations.literal: Soldiers who exerted themselves to the utmost were never rewarded; common people who were innocent all suffered slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who fought their hardest went unrewarded; innocent civilians were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 黎庶憤怨，天下土崩，至於就擒而猶未之寤也。

translations.literal: The common people were angry and resentful; the realm collapsed like crumbling earth; even when he was captured he still did not awaken.
translations.idiomatic: The people seethed with rage, the realm crumbled, and even when capture was at hand he still would not see it.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：煬帝爰在弱齡，早有令聞，南平吳、會，北却匈奴，昆弟之中，獨著聲績。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When Emperor Yang was in his youth, he already had a fine reputation — pacifying Wu and Kuai in the south, repelling the Xiongnu in the north; among his brothers he alone stood out in achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: In youth Emperor Yang already enjoyed a fine reputation — he pacified Wu and Kuai in the south and drove back the Xiongnu in the north, outshining all his brothers.

sentences.zh: 於是矯情飾貌，肆厥姦回，故得獻后鍾心，文皇革慮，天方肇亂，遂登儲兩，踐峻極之崇基，承丕顯之休命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he feigned sentiment and adorned his appearance, unleashing his treachery — thus winning Empress Xian's heart and changing Emperor Wen's mind; Heaven was just beginning disorder, yet he ascended the heirship, treading the lofty foundation of the supreme peak and inheriting the glorious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned virtue and hid his malice, won Empress Xian's heart and turned Emperor Wen's mind, and amid rising chaos ascended the throne to inherit the glorious mandate.

sentences.zh: 地廣三代，威振八紘，單于頓顙，越裳重譯。

translations.literal: His territory exceeded the Three Dynasties; his might shook the eight directions; the chanyu bowed his forehead; the Yuechang came through repeated translation.
translations.idiomatic: His domain outstripped the Three Dynasties, his might shook the eight directions, the chanyu bowed low, and distant Yuechang sent tribute through many translators.

sentences.zh: 赤仄之泉，流溢于都內，紅腐之粟，委積於塞下。

translations.literal: Red-edge coins overflowed within the capital; red-rotted grain piled up below the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: Copper cash overflowed in the capital; grain rotted in heaps below the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 負其富強之資，思逞無厭之欲，狹殷、周之制度，尚秦、漢之規摹。

translations.literal: Relying on his resources of wealth and strength, he thought to indulge desires without limit; he narrowed the institutions of Yin and Zhou and exalted the scale of Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Flush with wealth and power, he indulged boundless desire, narrowed Yin and Zhou institutions, and exalted Qin and Han scale.

sentences.zh: 恃才矜己，傲狠明德，內懷險躁，外示凝簡，盛冠服以飾其姦，除諫官以掩其過。

translations.literal: Trusting in his talent and praising himself, he was arrogant and harsh toward bright virtue; inwardly he harbored danger and impatience, outwardly he showed solemn simplicity; he piled cap and robe to adorn his treachery and removed remonstrance officials to cover his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant and self-admiring, harsh toward the virtuous, inwardly restless yet outwardly grave, he dressed his treachery in ceremony and silenced remonstrance officials to hide his faults.

sentences.zh: 淫荒無度，法令滋章，教絕四維，刑參五虐，鋤誅骨肉，屠勦忠良，受賞者莫見其功，為戮者不知其罪。

translations.literal: Licentious and unrestrained without limit, laws and orders multiplied; the four bonds of teaching were severed and punishments matched the five cruelties; he uprooted and executed kin, slaughtered and exterminated the loyal and good; those rewarded saw no merit, those executed knew no crime.
translations.idiomatic: Licentious beyond measure, he multiplied laws, severed the four bonds of teaching, and matched the five cruelties; he killed kin and slaughtered the loyal — the rewarded saw no merit, the executed knew no crime.

sentences.zh: 驕怒之兵屢動，土木之功不息，頻出朔方，三駕遼左，旌旗萬里，徵稅百端，猾吏侵漁，人不堪命。

translations.literal: Armies of arrogant wrath moved repeatedly; earth-and-wood works never ceased; he frequently went forth to Shuofang and thrice visited the Liao region; banners and flags stretched ten thousand li; levies had a hundred forms; cunning officials preyed on the people — men could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: His wrathful armies marched again and again, construction never ceased, he repeatedly visited Shuofang and thrice campaigned to the Liao, banners stretched ten thousand li, taxes took a hundred forms, and corrupt officials preyed until men could not endure.

sentences.zh: 乃急令暴條以擾之，嚴刑峻法以臨之，甲兵威武以董之，自是海內騷然，無聊生矣。

translations.literal: Then he issued urgent orders and violent statutes to harass them, applied harsh punishments and severe laws to oversee them, and used armor and weapons and martial might to compel them — from this the empire was in turmoil and none could live.
translations.idiomatic: He answered with urgent edicts and savage statutes, harsh laws and armed coercion — and the empire erupted in turmoil until none could live.

sentences.zh: 俄而玄感肇黎陽之亂，匈奴有雁門之圍，天子方棄中土，遠之揚、越。

translations.literal: Soon Xuangan raised rebellion at Liyang; the Xiongnu besieged at Yanmen; the Son of Heaven was just then abandoning the central lands and going far to Yang and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xuangan rebelled at Liyang, the Turks besieged Yanmen, and the emperor abandoned the heartland for distant Yang and Yue.

sentences.zh: 姦宄乘釁，強弱相陵，關梁閉而不通，皇輿往而不反。

translations.literal: Evildoers seized the opportunity; strong and weak oppressed one another; passes and bridges were closed and impassable; the imperial carriage went forth and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Evildoers seized their chance, the strong crushed the weak, passes closed, and the imperial carriage departed never to return.

sentences.zh: 加之以師旅，因之以饑饉，流離道路，轉死溝壑，十八九焉。

translations.literal: Added to this were armies on campaign and famine following in turn; people wandered on the roads and died turning in ditches and ravines — eight or nine out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Armies marched and famine followed; refugees died in ditches — eight or nine out of ten.

sentences.zh: 於是相聚萑蒲，蝟毛而起，大則跨州連郡，稱帝稱王，小則千百為羣，攻城剽邑，流血成川澤，死人如亂麻，炊者不及析骸，食者不遑易子。

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered in the marshes and rose like hedgehog quills; the great crossed commanderies and linked prefectures, styling themselves emperors and kings; the small formed groups of hundreds and thousands, attacking cities and raiding towns — blood flowed like rivers and lakes, the dead like tangled hemp; those who cooked had no time to divide corpses, those who ate had no leisure to exchange children.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered in the wilds and rose like quills; great rebels crossed commanderies and proclaimed themselves kings, small bands of hundreds stormed towns — blood ran like rivers, corpses piled like hemp; the living cooked the dead and ate their own children.

sentences.zh: 茫茫九土，並為麋鹿之場，𢛐𢛐黔黎，俱充蛇豕之餌。

translations.literal: The vast nine regions all became fields for deer; the anxious common people all became bait for serpents and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: The vast realm became a deer park; the common people became fodder for beasts.

sentences.zh: 四方萬里，簡書相續，猶謂鼠竊狗盜，不足為虞，上下相蒙，莫肯念亂，振蜉蝣之羽，窮長夜之樂。

translations.literal: From the four directions, ten thousand li, dispatches followed in succession — yet he still called them rat thieves and dog bandits, not worth worrying over; superiors and subordinates deceived one another, none willing to think on the chaos; he fluttered mayfly wings and exhausted the pleasures of the long night.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatches poured in from ten thousand li, yet he still dismissed the rebels as petty thieves; court and country lied to one another while he fluttered like a mayfly through endless nights of pleasure.

sentences.zh: 土崩魚爛，貫盈惡稔，普天之下，莫匪仇讎，左右之人，皆為敵國。

translations.literal: Earth crumbled and fish rotted; evil was full to the brim; under all heaven none were not enemies; those at his side all became hostile states.
translations.idiomatic: The realm crumbled, his evil was ripe; under heaven all were enemies, and even those at his side became foes.

sentences.zh: 終然不悟，同彼望夷，遂以萬乘之尊，死於一夫之手。

translations.literal: To the end he did not awaken, sharing the fate of Wang E — and so with the honor of ten thousand chariots, he died at the hands of a single man.
translations.idiomatic: He never awakened, shared Wang E's fate, and died by a single assassin's hand though he bore the honor of ten thousand chariots.

sentences.zh: 億兆靡感恩之士，九牧無勤王之師。

translations.literal: Among the hundred million there were none who felt gratitude; among the nine provinces there were no armies rushing to save the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Not one in the hundred million felt gratitude; not one of the nine provinces sent armies to save him.

sentences.zh: 子弟同就誅夷，骸骨棄而莫掩，社稷顛隕，本枝殄絕，自肇有書契以迄于茲，宇宙崩離，生靈塗炭，喪身滅國，未有若斯之甚也。

translations.literal: Sons and younger brothers together met execution and extermination; bones were abandoned and none covered them; the altars of soil and grain toppled; the root and branches were extinguished — from the beginning of written records down to the present, the cosmos split apart, living beings were smeared with charcoal, body lost and state destroyed — never has it been so extreme as this.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and brothers were executed together, bones lay unburied, the altars fell, the dynasty's root and branches were severed — since records began, never had collapse and ruin gone so far.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「天作孽，猶可違，自作孽，不可逭。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "When Heaven sends down calamity, it can still be avoided; when one brings calamity on oneself, it cannot be escaped."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: "Heaven's calamity may still be avoided; self-made calamity cannot be escaped."

sentences.zh: 」傳曰：「吉凶由人，祅不妄作。

translations.literal: The Tradition says: "Fortune and misfortune depend on men; portents do not arise without cause."
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition says: "Fortune and misfortune lie with men; omens do not arise without cause."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「兵猶火也，不戢將自焚。

translations.literal: It also says: "War is like fire; if it is not checked, it will burn the one who wields it."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "War is like fire; unchecked, it burns the hand that holds it."

sentences.zh: 」觀隋室之存亡，斯言信而有徵矣！

translations.literal: Observing the survival and destruction of the Sui house, these words are trustworthy and have proof!
translations.idiomatic: Looking at the Sui dynasty's rise and fall, these words are proven true!

sentences.zh: 舊唐書梁師都傳、又建成傳，新唐書梁師都傳，通鑑唐紀五作「劉仚成」；

translations.literal: Old Book of Tang, Biography of Liang Shidu, and also the Biography of Li Jiancheng; New Book of Tang, Biography of Liang Shidu; Zizhi Tongjian Tang Annals 5 write "Liu Xincheng";
translations.idiomatic: The Old Book of Tang biographies of Liang Shidu and Li Jiancheng, the New Book of Tang biography of Liang Shidu, and Zizhi Tongjian Tang Annals 5 read "Liu Xincheng";

sentences.zh: 冊府四四九、九七七、九八五作「劉企成」。

translations.literal: Imperial Archives 449, 977, and 985 write "Liu Qicheng."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Archives 449, 977, and 985 read "Liu Qicheng."

sentences.zh: 「仚」是「企」的別體字。

translations.literal: "Xian" is a variant form of "qi."
translations.idiomatic: The character xian is a variant form of qi.

sentences.zh: 今改。

translations.literal: Now changed.
translations.idiomatic: Emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 九月己丑 此月己酉朔，無己丑。

translations.literal: Jichou day of the ninth month: This month's first day is jiyou; there is no jichou.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day of the ninth month: with jiyou as the month's first day, there is no jichou.

sentences.zh: 日干有誤。

translations.literal: The day stem is in error.
translations.idiomatic: The day stem is wrong.

sentences.zh: 孟景 「景」應作「秉」。

translations.literal: Meng Jing: "Jing" should read "Bing."
translations.idiomatic: On Meng Jing: "Jing" should read "Bing."

sentences.zh: 唐人諱「昞」，因「秉」、「昞」同音，遂改「秉」為「景」。

translations.literal: The Tang tabooed the character for Emperor Taizong's personal name; because bing and the taboo form were homophones, bing was changed to jing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang taboo for Emperor Taizong's personal name, the homophone bing in the original name was written as jing.
